title: SOC Shift Command
blurb: Run the 23:00 to 07:00 shift. Pick your specialty, rack two tools, hold eight systems against a live adversary, and close out with a graded shift report.
source: Rewritten from a classified practice corpus; concepts per Chapple CISSP SG 10ed and the April-2024 exam outline

campaign.title: SOC Shift Command
campaign.prompt: Eight systems, one 15-hour night shift. Pick your specialty and rack two tools — every system shows its price before you touch it, and every miss becomes a live incident you must contain.

config.maxGateRatioNote: beta.1 ships at 0.67 against its own 0.60 cap: the tiers average two gate cards per board decision. Recorded, not fixed, and deliberately not fixed by moving the cap — 0.60 is the number the design argued for. Bringing the deck under it means fewer cards per gate, or the deeper containment loop design R4 names as the real mitigation. Both are content work for the next wave.

roles.name: Identity analyst
roles.definition: You live in the authentication and authorization plane: sign-in telemetry, factor challenges, federation assertions, privilege changes. Nights on your watch tilt toward stolen credentials and quiet permission creep, because that is the traffic you can actually read.

roles.name: Network analyst
roles.definition: You read flows, not files: segmentation maps, egress patterns, beacon intervals, protocol misuse. Your shift bends toward probes, pivots, and callbacks — the adversary moves you can see on the wire.

roles.name: Endpoint analyst
roles.definition: You work the hosts: process trees, persistence keys, driver loads, tamper alerts. Malware that runs, hides, or digs in surfaces on your queue first — the wire and the boardroom are someone else's problem.

roles.name: GRC analyst
roles.definition: You hold the paper line: control evidence, audit trails, notification duties, executive risk questions. Your nights fill with auditors and anxious leadership — and when an incident lands, you are the one who knows what must be reported, to whom, by when.

territories.name: Governance desk
territories.teach: The Governance desk holds Domain 1: ethics, security concepts, governance and accountability, legal and regulatory duty, policy structure, BC requirements, personnel security, risk management, threat modeling, supply chain, and awareness.

territories.name: Asset vault
territories.teach: The Asset vault holds Domain 2: classification, ownership, handling, provisioning, lifecycle and retention, end-of-life disposal, and the data-state controls (DLP, CASB, DRM) that keep assets where they belong.

territories.name: Architecture rack
territories.teach: The Architecture rack holds Domain 3: secure design principles, security models, control selection, hardware taxonomy, architecture vulnerabilities, cryptography and its attacks, and site and facility engineering.

territories.name: Network core
territories.teach: The Network core holds Domain 4: architecture and segmentation, network components and hardening, and the secure channels — IPsec, TLS, VPN — that traffic must survive transit inside.

territories.name: Identity plane
territories.teach: The Identity plane holds Domain 5: physical and logical access, IAAA design, federation and trust direction, authorization models from DAC to ABAC, the provisioning lifecycle, and authentication systems including biometrics, Kerberos, and MFA.

territories.name: Assurance bench
territories.teach: The Assurance bench holds Domain 6: assessment and audit strategy, control testing from scans to penetration tests, security process data and KPIs, analysis of outputs, and the SOC report family.

territories.name: Ops floor
territories.teach: The Ops floor holds Domain 7 — the largest ward on the map: forensics and custody, logging and SIEM, configuration and change management, separation of duties, media protection, the incident lifecycle, detection tooling, patching, recovery strategies, DR process and testing, BCP exercises, physical security, and life safety.

territories.name: Dev pipeline
territories.teach: The Dev pipeline holds Domain 8: SDLC methodologies and maturity models, development ecosystem and CI/CD controls, the software testing taxonomy, acquired software risk, and secure coding against the OWASP classics.

cards.q: A hospital record system shows a VIP patient's admission reason as 'routine checkup' to general staff, while clinicians with elevated clearance see the true diagnosis stored in a separate copy of the same record. What is this database security technique called?
cards.answer: Polyinstantiation
cards.why: Polyinstantiation stores two or more versions of the same data item, so what a subject sees depends on that subject's clearance level, keeping the real record hidden from lower-cleared viewers.

cards.q: A gallery wants a sensor that trips an alarm when the electrostatic field surrounding a protected sculpture is disturbed. Which motion-detection technology should be installed?
cards.answer: Capacitance
cards.why: Capacitance detectors monitor the electromagnetic field around a specific protected object and alarm when that field is disturbed, unlike heat, wave, or beam-based sensors.

cards.q: An attacker captures session tokens off the wire today and plans to reuse them against the application in 48 hours. What attack is she preparing?
cards.answer: Replay attack
cards.why: Capturing legitimate credentials or session tokens and reusing them later to impersonate the original session is the defining trait of a replay attack.

cards.q: A group of regional credit unions with similar compliance needs wants to jointly host a fraud-detection platform, sharing the cost and infrastructure only among themselves. Which cloud deployment model fits best?
cards.answer: Community cloud
cards.why: A community cloud is built for a defined group of organizations that share common interests or compliance requirements and jointly fund and use the shared environment.

cards.q: In the classic four-ring protection model, at which ring do ordinary user applications typically execute?
cards.answer: Ring 3
cards.why: Most operating systems use only ring 0 for the trusted kernel and ring 3 for untrusted user-mode applications, leaving rings 1 and 2 largely unused in practice.

cards.q: Which historical cipher shifts each letter a fixed number of places through the alphabet, with the receiver shifting back the same amount?
cards.answer: Caesar cipher
cards.why: The Caesar cipher is a simple substitution cipher that shifts every letter by a fixed number of positions in the alphabet.

cards.q: When scouting a site for a new data center, which factor is NOT a legitimate physical security consideration?
options: How scenic the surrounding area is
cards.answer: How scenic the surrounding area is
cards.why: Site selection weighs utilities, natural hazards like flooding, and crime, but the visual appeal of the area has no bearing on the site's security posture.

cards.q: What is a Distributed Control System (DCS) primarily used for?
options: Centralized monitoring of servers and workstations
Computerized control of an industrial process or plant with distributed autonomous controllers
cards.answer: Computerized control of an industrial process or plant with distributed autonomous controllers
cards.why: A DCS distributes autonomous controllers throughout a plant or process while still allowing centralized operator supervision, unlike a purely centralized SCADA-style setup.

cards.q: A firm applies a different set of security controls at its headquarters than it does at its branch offices, tailored to each site's own risk profile. What approach is this?
cards.answer: Differentiated security controls
cards.why: Differentiated security controls tailor the type and strength of controls to the specific risk and requirements of each location, rather than applying one uniform baseline everywhere.

cards.q: Under Bell-LaPadula's simple security property, what is a subject prohibited from doing?
options: Modifying a file at a higher classification
Reading a file at a higher classification
Reading a file at a lower classification
Accessing a file at the same classification
cards.answer: Reading a file at a higher classification
cards.why: The simple security property enforces 'no read up': a subject may not read data classified above its own clearance level.

cards.q: Fences and gates around a facility are primarily meant to accomplish what?
options: Let staff exit quickly during an emergency
Funnel entry and exit through a small number of controlled points
Block staff from safely exiting in an emergency
Provide easy, unrestricted access to the site
cards.answer: Funnel entry and exit through a small number of controlled points
cards.why: Fences and gates work together to restrict all foot and vehicle traffic to a limited number of monitored entry points rather than open access anywhere along the perimeter.

cards.q: An analyst running a digraph attack against ciphertext is looking for what?
options: How often specific pairs of letters appear
cards.answer: How often specific pairs of letters appear
cards.why: A digraph attack extends frequency analysis to look at how often common letter pairs, like TH or HE, occur in the ciphertext.

cards.q: In which cloud service model is the customer responsible for the operating system and everything above it?
cards.answer: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
cards.why: With IaaS the provider stops at the hardware and virtualization layer, leaving the customer to install and manage the OS and everything running on top of it.

cards.q: Which CPU component directs the fetching and execution of instructions?
cards.answer: Control Unit (CU)
cards.why: The control unit coordinates fetching instructions from memory and directing their execution across the ALU and registers, rather than performing the arithmetic itself.

cards.q: One-time pads are mathematically unbreakable, yet they are rarely used commercially. What is the main practical reason why?
options: Each pad has to hold as many symbols as the message it protects
The key can never be reused
The key must be kept fully secret between parties
cards.answer: Each pad has to hold as many symbols as the message it protects
cards.why: Because the pad has to be as long as the message and can only be used once, securely distributing enough pad material for ongoing communication is impractical at scale.

cards.q: Which of these is NOT a valid method for mitigating electromagnetic interference (EMI) in electronic equipment?
cards.answer: Incinerating the device
cards.why: Shielding, grounding, and filtering all reduce or redirect unwanted electromagnetic energy, while destroying the device is not a mitigation technique at all.

cards.q: A logistics alliance of shippers, customs brokers, and warehouse operators wants a shared ledger where only alliance members validate transactions, rather than one company controlling it or the public having open access. Which blockchain type best fits?
cards.answer: Federated (consortium) blockchain
cards.why: A federated blockchain is governed by a defined set of cooperating organizations rather than a single owner or the open public, which matches a multi-party alliance's needs for shared control and selective transparency.

cards.q: A company wants headquarters-to-branch traffic protected so that both packet headers and payload are encrypted, but each intermediate network node decrypts and re-encrypts the traffic before forwarding it onward. Which technique does this describe?
cards.answer: Link encryption
cards.why: Link encryption protects an entire packet, including headers, but requires decryption and re-encryption at every hop, unlike end-to-end encryption which stays encrypted from source to destination.

cards.q: An auditor at a consultancy must never access a competing client's data once she has worked on a given client's engagement, and the system enforces this dynamically based on her access history. Which security model implements this 'Chinese wall'?
cards.answer: Brewer-Nash
cards.why: The Brewer-Nash model dynamically adjusts a subject's permitted access based on what that subject has already accessed, specifically to prevent conflicts of interest between competing clients.

cards.q: Why are virtualized environments fundamentally exposed to a class of attack that physically separated server farms are not?
options: Inherent complexity of the hypervisor software
Multiple VMs sharing the same underlying physical resources
cards.answer: Multiple VMs sharing the same underlying physical resources
cards.why: Because several virtual machines share one host's processor, memory, and storage, a compromise that escapes one VM can potentially reach the hypervisor and every other tenant on that host.

cards.q: Priya is hardening physical security for her company's data center, assuming a determined attacker can eventually defeat any single control. What overall design approach should guide her?
cards.answer: Layered, defense-in-depth physical controls
cards.why: Because any individual barrier, lock, or badge system can eventually be bypassed, effective physical security depends on multiple overlapping layers that compensate for each other's weaknesses.

cards.q: A storage engineer configures RAID striping with parity for redundancy. What is the minimum number of disks required?
cards.why: Striping alone needs only two disks and provides no redundancy; adding a parity disk for redundancy raises the minimum to three.

cards.q: Researchers break a cryptosystem purely by observing changes in power draw, memory usage, and electromagnetic emissions during encryption, without altering any inputs or tapping the algorithm directly. What kind of attack is this?
cards.answer: Side-channel attack
cards.why: A side-channel attack is passive: it infers secrets from physical emanations like power, timing, or electromagnetic radiation rather than exploiting a flaw in the algorithm or actively interfering with the device.

cards.q: An online gaming platform processes most gameplay on mini servers physically close to each cluster of players for minimal latency, while only payment transactions are routed to a single centralized server. What deployment model does this describe?
cards.answer: Edge computing
cards.why: Edge computing pushes most processing onto devices or servers close to the end user, sending only the data that truly needs central handling, such as transactions, back to a core server.

cards.q: Which of the following provides the strongest security per key length for generating digital signatures?
cards.answer: ECDSA
cards.why: ECDSA achieves an equivalent or stronger security margin than RSA or DSA using much shorter keys, while MD5 is a broken hash function unsuitable for signatures at all.

cards.q: The Graham-Denning model defines a fixed set of operations a subject can perform on an object. Which operation is absent from that set?
cards.answer: Create access
cards.why: Graham-Denning's eight defined rules include creating and destroying subjects and objects plus transferring, granting, and deleting access, but 'create access' as a standalone operation is not one of them.

cards.q: What best distinguishes the security responsibilities of a private cloud from those of a public cloud?
options: Public clouds are inherently more secure due to scale, while private clouds are inherently weaker
Private clouds always outsource security to a third party, public clouds never do
In a private cloud the organization owns all security responsibility; in a public cloud, responsibility is shared with the provider
Public cloud security focuses only on data segregation while private cloud focuses only on physical security
cards.answer: In a private cloud the organization owns all security responsibility; in a public cloud, responsibility is shared with the provider
cards.why: A private cloud leaves the owning organization fully accountable for every layer of security, while public clouds operate under a shared responsibility model splitting duties between provider and customer.

cards.q: A vendor advertises its VPN appliance as Common Criteria EAL7 certified. What does this certification actually confirm?
options: The product is automatically the right fit for your organization
The product met the functionality and assurance requirements of its Protection Profile
The product satisfies every functional and non-functional requirement your organization has
The product is secure no matter how users behave
cards.answer: The product met the functionality and assurance requirements of its Protection Profile
cards.why: Common Criteria certification confirms that an independent lab validated the product against a specific Protection Profile's functional and assurance criteria; it does not guarantee fitness for your organization's particular needs.

cards.q: A colleague worries that brute force could theoretically crack a properly used one-time pad. Should this concern change your security posture?
options: Yes, the attacker would recover the actual key
No, brute-forcing a one-time pad yields so many equally plausible plaintexts that the result is useless
Brute force cannot be applied to one-time pads at all
Yes, once broken, the one-time pad becomes worthless
cards.answer: No, brute-forcing a one-time pad yields so many equally plausible plaintexts that the result is useless
cards.why: Trying every possible key against a true one-time pad produces every possible plaintext of that length, so the attacker cannot distinguish the real message from the noise.

cards.q: A new cloud provider is drafting marketing copy listing its service model offerings. Which of the following is actually a deployment model, not a service model, and so should NOT appear on that list?
options: Pre-configured VMs for developers to upload source code to
Bare virtual machines with no OS or applications preinstalled
A dedicated cloud environment offered exclusively to one company
cards.answer: A dedicated cloud environment offered exclusively to one company
cards.why: An environment dedicated to a single customer describes a private cloud deployment model, which is a different concept from the SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS service models the other options represent.

cards.q: A sender hashes a message, signs the hash with her private key, and appends it to the plaintext. The recipient decrypts the signature with her public key, recomputes the hash, and compares the two. What security services does this process BEST provide?
cards.answer: Authentication, Integrity, Non-repudiation
cards.why: Signing a hash with a private key proves who sent the message and that it was not altered, and prevents the sender from later denying it; the plaintext itself is not encrypted, so confidentiality is not provided.

cards.q: A bank chooses the Clark-Wilson model to protect the integrity of transactional data. Which two principles does the model rely on?
options: Least privilege and separation of duties
Well-formed transactions and separation of duties
cards.answer: Well-formed transactions and separation of duties
cards.why: Clark-Wilson forces all changes through controlled, well-formed transactions and splits critical tasks among multiple roles via separation of duties, together preventing unauthorized or inconsistent modification of data.

cards.q: While auditing a database, Marco finds column values that do not match the declared data type for that field. What kind of integrity violation is this?
cards.answer: Semantic integrity
cards.why: Semantic integrity requires each stored value to be consistent with its declared attribute type, which is exactly what is violated when a field holds data of the wrong type.

cards.q: Security engineers want firmware storage that survives a reboot, can still be updated when genuinely needed, yet resists being silently rewritten by a remote attacker the way electrically-reprogrammable memory can. Which memory type best fits?
cards.answer: EPROM
cards.why: EPROM is non-volatile like ROM but can be reprogrammed, and unlike EEPROM its erasure requires physical intervention rather than a purely electronic, remotely-triggerable write.

cards.q: How do cloud security architecture and cloud security design differ?
options: Architecture designs and implements measures, while design manages and maintains them
Architecture is the overall blueprint for the security system, while design implements specific measures within it
Architecture manages the security of the environment, while design is purely technical implementation
Architecture is a written set of rules, while design is simply carrying those rules out on the hardware
cards.answer: Architecture is the overall blueprint for the security system, while design implements specific measures within it
cards.why: Cloud security architecture lays out the high-level structure and principles for protecting the environment, while cloud security design turns that blueprint into specific, configured controls.

cards.q: Before authorizing a payment, a shopper wants real-time confirmation that a merchant's TLS certificate has not been revoked, without relying on a periodically-downloaded list that may lag behind. Which mechanism satisfies this?
cards.answer: Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP)
cards.why: OCSP queries the certificate authority directly for a certificate's current status, giving a real-time answer instead of the delayed snapshot a downloaded CRL provides.

cards.q: A Top Secret-cleared officer can edit a joint case file that a Secret-cleared officer is also working on, but the Secret-cleared officer cannot write to a document owned by the Top Secret officer. Which Biba rule explains this?
cards.answer: Star Integrity Property
cards.why: Biba's star integrity property blocks a subject from writing to an object at a higher integrity level, which is why the lower-cleared officer cannot modify the higher officer's document.

cards.q: When migrating from physical servers to a virtualized environment, what is the most significant new security concern introduced?
options: Malware spreading across VMs on the same host
cards.answer: Unauthorized access to the hypervisor
cards.why: The hypervisor mediates every virtual machine on the host, so an attacker who compromises it can potentially reach and control every VM and its data, making it the single highest-impact target introduced by virtualization.

cards.q: An e-commerce CISO is redesigning the company's website architecture from scratch to handle rapid growth. What should be prioritized in the design itself, rather than added afterward?
options: A secure-by-design approach built into the architecture from the start
Deploying cutting-edge intrusion detection and prevention tooling
cards.answer: A secure-by-design approach built into the architecture from the start
cards.why: Building security into the architecture from the outset addresses root-cause vulnerabilities, while patching, firewalls, and IDS/IPS are reactive layers that respond to problems after the fact.

cards.q: During which stage does the IKE protocol first establish its secure negotiation channel?
cards.answer: Security association
cards.why: The security association phase is where the two devices first agree on encryption and authentication parameters and establish the secure tunnel that later phases use.

cards.q: A bank wants transactions modifiable only through controlled intermediary programs, using well-formed transactions and separation of duties to guarantee data integrity. Which model fits?
cards.answer: Clark-Wilson model
cards.why: The Clark-Wilson model enforces integrity by requiring all modifications to pass through restricted, well-formed transaction programs and by dividing critical steps among separate roles.

cards.q: Which of these is a common attack specifically against data while it is in use, rather than at rest or in transit?
options: A gap in the business continuity plan
cards.answer: Screen-scraping malware
cards.why: Screen scrapers capture data as it is being rendered or processed on screen, which is precisely the data-in-use state, unlike attacks aimed at stored or in-transit data.

cards.q: A CISO wants full control over application code and configuration while outsourcing the underlying servers, OS, and infrastructure entirely to a vendor. Which cloud service model fits?
options: Remaining fully on-premises with no cloud usage
cards.answer: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
cards.why: PaaS lets the customer build, control, and deploy applications while the provider manages the underlying infrastructure, OS, and platform, matching the stated split of responsibility.

cards.q: When rolling out digital certificates for secure communications, what is the single most important factor to get right?
options: The trustworthiness of the issuing certificate authority
The size of the IT security team
Whether certificates are labeled SSL or TLS type
cards.answer: The trustworthiness of the issuing certificate authority
cards.why: Every certificate's value depends on the issuing CA being trustworthy; if the CA itself is compromised or untrustworthy, renewal frequency and other details cannot compensate.

cards.q: A Top Secret-cleared detective is barred from adding notes to a case file classified only 'Confidential,' even though a Confidential-cleared officer can freely add to that same file. Which Bell-LaPadula rule explains the detective's restriction?
cards.answer: Star Security Property
cards.why: The star property enforces 'no write down,' preventing a subject with higher clearance from writing to an object at a lower classification, to stop sensitive information from leaking downward.

cards.q: Malware modifies the operating system to plant an undocumented command sequence that lets the attacker bypass normal restrictions and reach a victim's files at will. What has been installed?
cards.answer: A back door
cards.why: A back door is an undocumented access mechanism embedded in a system that lets someone who knows about it bypass normal authentication and restrictions.

cards.q: A researcher feeds raw transaction data into an algorithm that must find suspicious patterns on its own, with no labeled 'fraud' or 'not fraud' outcomes provided in advance. What type of AI system is this?
cards.answer: An unsupervised machine learning system
cards.why: Unsupervised learning finds structure and patterns in data without being given labeled correct answers, unlike supervised learning which trains on pre-labeled examples.

cards.q: An author wants to prove that a manuscript sent to a publisher was not altered in transit and that it genuinely came from her. Which combination achieves this?
options: Public key cryptography plus symmetric cryptography
Public key cryptography plus a hashing algorithm
Shared key cryptography plus a hashing algorithm
cards.answer: Public key cryptography plus a hashing algorithm
cards.why: Hashing the document and signing that hash with a private key lets the recipient verify both authenticity and integrity using the sender's public key, without needing a securely pre-shared secret.

cards.q: What is typically the FIRST visible indicator that a cloud migration has gone well?
options: The highest achievable level of data security
The most efficient possible resource utilization
cards.answer: Minimal downtime experienced by users
cards.why: Business continuity during the cutover is the immediate, observable measure of a smooth migration, while cost savings, optimized resource use, and mature security posture only become evident over time.

cards.q: What matters most when implementing Software-Defined Security (SDSec)?
options: A risk-based approach to security decisions
cards.answer: A risk-based approach to security decisions
cards.why: SDSec's value lies in rapidly adapting security controls, but that agility only helps if decisions about what to prioritize and automate are grounded in an ongoing assessment of risk.

cards.q: For a given level of cryptographic strength, which public-key method achieves it with the shortest, most efficient keys?
cards.answer: Elliptic curve cryptography
cards.why: ECC's security relies on the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem, which is hard enough that ECC matches RSA or DSA security using much shorter, more efficient keys.

cards.q: A firm wants to offload hardware maintenance and OS patching to a vendor but retain full control of its own applications and data, at the lowest reasonable cost. Which combination of deployment and service model fits best?
cards.answer: Public cloud - PaaS
cards.why: PaaS shifts hardware and patching duties to the provider while leaving applications and data under the customer's control, and a public cloud deployment keeps costs lowest among the shared models.

cards.q: An organization keeps sensitive workloads on-premises but spreads its less-sensitive workloads across several different public cloud vendors specifically to avoid depending on any single provider. What is this strategy called?
cards.answer: Multi-cloud
cards.why: Multi-cloud specifically means deliberately using more than one public cloud service provider, which distinguishes it from a hybrid setup that simply blends public and private clouds.

cards.q: For 100 employees who all need to communicate securely with each other pairwise, which approach requires the larger total number of keys, symmetric or asymmetric?
options: They require the same number of keys
cards.answer: Symmetric
cards.why: Pairwise symmetric encryption needs a unique key for every pair of users, growing roughly with the square of the population, while asymmetric encryption needs only one key pair per user.

cards.q: A cloud architect needs a control point that sits between her organization and its cloud provider to enforce the company's own security policies on cloud traffic. What should she deploy?
cards.answer: A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB)
cards.why: A CASB is deployed as a policy enforcement point between the cloud consumer and the cloud service provider, applying the customer's own security requirements to cloud traffic.

cards.q: After disabling SSLv3 in favor of TLS 1.2 to remediate a POODLE finding, how many distinct keys are, at minimum, involved in establishing and using a TLS 1.2 session?
cards.why: TLS 1.2 involves at least a server public key and matching private key for identification and key exchange, plus a negotiated symmetric session key used to encrypt the actual data.

cards.q: An attacker steals password hash values from a compromised admin account and replays those hashes directly to authenticate to other systems, without ever cracking the hash. What attack technique is this?
cards.answer: Pass-the-Hash (PtH) attack
cards.why: A Pass-the-Hash attack authenticates using the captured hash value itself, never needing to recover the underlying plaintext password.

cards.q: Employees keep emailing sensitive data in cleartext despite an existing policy against it. What is the most reliable technical fix?
options: Train employees to manually encrypt sensitive emails
Adopt a third-party encryption service employees must remember to use
Deploy software that automatically encrypts sensitive outbound email without relying on user action
Ban sending sensitive data by email entirely
cards.answer: Deploy software that automatically encrypts sensitive outbound email without relying on user action
cards.why: Automatic encryption removes the dependency on employees remembering to act correctly every time, closing the gap that training and opt-in tools both leave open.

cards.q: Without clipping levels in place, which countermeasure best slows a brute-force attack against a password by adding real computational delay to every guess?
cards.answer: Key stretching
cards.why: Key stretching deliberately adds processing time to each password verification attempt, which multiplies the total time needed for a brute-force attack across millions of guesses.

cards.q: Before two IPSec endpoints can exchange protected traffic, they must agree on key lengths, algorithms, mode of operation, and hash functions. What is this agreement called?
cards.answer: Security Association (SA)
cards.why: A Security Association is the negotiated set of parameters both IPSec endpoints agree to use, distinct from AH and ESP which are the protocols that apply those parameters to traffic.

cards.q: Briefed on a possible 0-day vulnerability in widely-used software, and mindful of lessons from the Stuxnet worm, what should a CISO prioritize to limit the impact of an exploit with no available patch?
options: Boosting intrusion detection to catch anomalous behavior alone
Strengthening defense-in-depth with overlapping security layers
cards.answer: Strengthening defense-in-depth with overlapping security layers
cards.why: Since a 0-day has no patch and may evade any single detection method, overlapping layers of controls increase the odds that some layer catches or contains the exploit even when others fail.

cards.q: A defense contractor handles Top Secret information split into compartments covering submarines, AI research, and space systems. How should access control be configured to enforce least privilege with maximum granularity?
options: Give every Top-Secret-cleared user the same blanket clearance
Use Discretionary Access Control and let data owners decide access case by case
Assign each user both a clearance level and specific compartment labels matching their exact work area
Use broad domain classifications with access based only on overall clearance level
cards.answer: Assign each user both a clearance level and specific compartment labels matching their exact work area
cards.why: Combining clearance level with compartment-specific labels ensures a user can only reach the exact subset of information relevant to their role, which is finer-grained than clearance alone or discretionary owner decisions.

cards.q: A procurement lead at Meridian Insurance is choosing a firewall under Common Criteria. She has a document listing everything the company needs the product to do, and each vendor has published a document describing the security functions actually built into its product. What are these two documents, respectively?
options: Target of evaluation and security assurance requirement
Evaluation assurance level and protection profile
cards.answer: Protection profile and security target
cards.why: Under Common Criteria (ISO/IEC 15408), the customer's statement of security needs is the protection profile (PP), while the vendor's statement of the security claims built into the target of evaluation is the security target (ST); procurement compares the PP against candidate STs and buys the closest match.

cards.q: An executive reviewing two Common Criteria certified VPN appliances assumes the EAL5 product must offer more security features than the EAL2 product and wants to buy it on that basis. How should the security architect correct this reasoning?
options: A higher EAL reflects a more rigorous evaluation of the product's claims, not a larger set of security functions
The executive is right: each EAL step adds mandatory security functionality to the product
EAL ratings only apply to government systems, so neither rating matters for a private firm
EAL2 always indicates the product failed part of its evaluation
cards.answer: A higher EAL reflects a more rigorous evaluation of the product's claims, not a larger set of security functions
cards.why: An evaluation assurance level rates the depth and rigor of the evaluation performed — from EAL1 (functionally tested) up to EAL7 (formally verified, designed, and tested). It measures confidence that the product does what its security target claims, not how many security features it has.

cards.q: While adapting a control baseline for a standalone engineering workstation that has no wireless hardware and never connects to a network, an analyst removes the baseline's wireless and remote-access controls because they cannot apply to this system. What is this activity called?
cards.answer: Scoping
cards.why: Scoping reviews a baseline and eliminates the controls that do not apply to the system at all — such as wireless controls on a machine with no radio. Tailoring, by contrast, adjusts the remaining applicable controls (parameters, compensating substitutions) to fit the organization's mission.

cards.q: A baseline requires host-based intrusion prevention agents, but Aldgate Rail's train-control endpoints cannot run the agent without violating the vendor's real-time safety certification. The security team instead adjusts the baseline for those endpoints, substituting network-level monitoring as a compensating control. What best describes this activity?
options: Tailoring the baseline to fit the organization's mission and constraints
Scoping out controls that do not apply to the system
Accepting the risk and documenting an exception with no control change
Re-categorizing the system at a lower impact level
cards.answer: Tailoring the baseline to fit the organization's mission and constraints
cards.why: Tailoring modifies a control baseline so it fits the specific environment — adjusting parameters and substituting compensating controls where a prescribed control is unworkable. The control still applies (unlike scoping, which removes inapplicable controls), so it is adapted rather than dropped.

cards.q: A government case-management system suffered a significant breach last month, and separately its three-year authorization window lapses next quarter. The system owner asks whether the existing authorization to operate (ATO) still stands. What is the correct position?
options: The ATO must be re-obtained now, because a significant security breach invalidates it regardless of the expiry date
The ATO remains valid until its expiry date because breaches do not affect authorization
Only the authorizing official's retirement can end an ATO early
An ATO never expires once granted; renewal is a courtesy
cards.answer: The ATO must be re-obtained now, because a significant security breach invalidates it regardless of the expiry date
cards.why: An authorization to operate reflects an authorizing official's acceptance of a known risk posture. That posture is voided by a significant security change or breach, so the ATO must be renewed at that point — not merely when the authorization period runs out.

cards.q: An architect redesigning a campus lobby makes the main entrance visually unmistakable, funnels visitors along a single path past the reception desk, and deliberately makes corridors to restricted wings feel harder to enter than the open collaboration areas. Which CPTED principle is being applied?
cards.answer: Natural access control
cards.why: Natural access control is CPTED's subtle guidance of movement: make the entry point obvious, create internal security zones, and let same-level areas feel open while restricted areas feel harder to reach. Surveillance is about observation; territorial reinforcement is about a cared-for, inclusive feel.
cards.citation: SG ch.10 'Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design' · outline 3.8

cards.q: After a string of after-hours break-in attempts, a facilities manager upgrades exterior lighting, replaces the enclosed stairwells with open ones, and clears shrubbery from around every entrance so anyone approaching can be seen from the street and neighboring offices. Which CPTED principle do these changes serve?
cards.answer: Natural surveillance
cards.why: Natural surveillance makes would-be intruders feel exposed by maximizing the chance of being observed — well-lit areas, open walkways and stairways, and unobstructed sightlines around entrances. It deters crime through visibility rather than by guiding movement or signaling ownership.
cards.citation: SG ch.10 'Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design' · outline 3.8

cards.q: During critical path analysis for a new operations facility, a planner notices that the design routes voice, data, building automation, and CCTV over a single converged IP backbone terminating in one room. From a secure facility planning perspective, what is the primary concern this convergence raises?
options: It merges formerly separate services onto one element whose failure or compromise takes everything down at once
Converged infrastructure is inherently non-compliant with fire codes
IP-based CCTV cannot be encrypted, so the design leaks video
It increases cabling costs beyond acceptable limits
cards.answer: It merges formerly separate services onto one element whose failure or compromise takes everything down at once
cards.why: Critical path analysis should evaluate technology convergence — the tendency of utilities, solutions, and systems to merge over time. When previously independent services ride one backbone, an outage or attack on that element takes them all down, creating a single point of failure that is also a richer target.
cards.citation: SG ch.10 'Secure Facility Plan / Critical Path Analysis' · outline 3.8

cards.q: A property manager for a shared research campus schedules prompt graffiti removal, keeps landscaping trimmed, repairs broken fixtures quickly, and adds community signage and gathering spaces so the grounds feel actively cared for. Under CPTED, what is the security rationale for this program?
options: A maintained, community-feeling space signals ownership and deters offenders who read disrepair as freedom to act with impunity
Clean facilities reduce the fire load and therefore the insurance premium
Landscaping changes primarily improve camera focal range
Upkeep is purely cosmetic and has no recognized security effect
cards.answer: A maintained, community-feeling space signals ownership and deters offenders who read disrepair as freedom to act with impunity
cards.why: Natural territorial reinforcement makes an area feel like an inclusive, cared-for community. CPTED holds that run-down property invites crime by suggesting nobody is watching or will respond, so upkeep and visible ownership are deliberate, passive crime-reduction features of site design.
cards.citation: SG ch.10 'Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design' · outline 3.8

cards.q: An adversary has recovered several encrypted messages from a courier along with the exact plaintext of two of them, obtained from a leaked archive. She now studies statistical relationships between those plaintext-ciphertext pairs to recover the key used for the remaining messages. What attack model is this?
cards.answer: Known plaintext attack
cards.why: In a known plaintext attack the analyst possesses matching plaintext and ciphertext pairs she did not choose, and exploits the statistical relationships between them (linear cryptanalysis is the classic technique) to deduce the key. Ciphertext-only gives no plaintext; chosen models let the attacker pick the inputs.

cards.q: A hardware security lab evaluates a payment card by briefly dropping the chip's supply voltage and firing precisely timed clock glitches while it computes signatures, hoping the induced computation errors expose key material. Which cryptanalytic attack class is the lab exercising?
cards.answer: Fault injection attack
cards.why: Fault injection deliberately stresses a device — voltage manipulation, clock glitching, temperature extremes — to force computational errors whose faulty outputs leak secrets. A timing attack only measures how long correct operations take; it never induces errors in the computation itself.

cards.q: A hospital's imaging systems cannot tolerate even the momentary transfer gap when backup power switches in. Which UPS design should the facilities engineer specify?
options: Double conversion, because equipment draws continuously from the battery with no switchover
Line-interactive, because the battery sits outside the power path until the grid fails
A surge protector chained to a standby generator
A power-line conditioner feeding the equipment directly from the grid
cards.answer: Double conversion, because equipment draws continuously from the battery with no switchover
cards.why: A double-conversion UPS takes wall power into a battery and feeds equipment from that battery continuously, so a grid failure causes no transfer gap; a line-interactive UPS keeps the battery out of line during normal conditions and must switch over when power drops.

cards.q: A data-center designer wants water-based fire suppression above the racks but worries a damaged sprinkler head could dump water onto live equipment. Which system design directly addresses that concern?
options: A pre-action system, which holds water back until a separate detection stage triggers
A wet pipe system, because its pipes are always charged and ready
A deluge system, because its larger pipes clear water faster
Replacing detection with more frequent fire-warden walkthroughs
cards.answer: A pre-action system, which holds water back until a separate detection stage triggers
cards.why: A pre-action system is a two-stage variation of the dry pipe design: water enters the pipes only after an independent detection event, so a single damaged sprinkler head cannot release water onto equipment — the reason it is favored where accidental discharge is costly.

cards.q: Server logs show equipment resets during an afternoon when utility voltage stayed measurably low for several hours before returning to normal. Which commercial power problem should the engineer name in the incident report?
options: A fault — momentary complete loss of power
An inrush — the surge when equipment first connects to power
cards.answer: A brownout — prolonged low voltage
cards.why: Power vocabulary matters when specifying countermeasures: a brownout is prolonged low voltage while a sag or dip is only momentary; a fault is a momentary total loss, and inrush is the initial current draw at connection — naming the event correctly drives whether a conditioner, UPS, or generator is the fix.

cards.q: Designing a high-assurance platform, an architect rejects relying on the operating system to keep each process's memory separate and instead wants separation enforced by physical controls mapping processes to dedicated memory. Which memory protection method is she specifying?
cards.answer: Hardware segmentation
cards.why: Process isolation is the OS providing logically separate memory spaces per process, while hardware segmentation forces separation through physical hardware controls, mapping processes to dedicated memory locations — the stronger guarantee sought in high-assurance designs.

cards.q: Vantage Health decommissions a batch of SSDs that once held patient records. Which method destroys the data most effectively?
cards.answer: Physical destruction
cards.why: SSDs store data across flash cells with no magnetic domains, so degaussing has no effect, and formatting or a single purge pass can leave recoverable cells; physically destroying the media is the only reliable way to eliminate remanence.

cards.q: A studio embeds hidden ownership data directly inside its video files to trace the source if a copy leaks. What is this technique called?
cards.answer: Digital watermarking
cards.why: Embedding an identifying marker inside media to trace ownership is watermarking; steganography hides an unrelated message, DLP blocks exfiltration, and a copyright notice is a separate textual claim, not embedded data.

cards.q: Meridian Bank is drafting its first data retention policy. What should the team decide FIRST?
options: How long to retain each dataset
Where retained data will be stored
cards.answer: Which data must be retained
cards.why: Retention duration, storage method, and enforcement ownership all depend on first scoping which data categories actually require retention.

cards.q: Cobalt Freight is migrating a large dataset to the cloud. Which method is SLOWEST?
options: An operator re-keys records into the new system by hand
cards.answer: An operator re-keys records into the new system by hand
cards.why: Hand re-keying depends on constant human effort and is bounded by how fast a person can type, making it the slowest option; automated, encrypted, and bulk-device transfers all move data with far less manual overhead.

cards.q: Which state describes data actively being processed in a running application's memory?
cards.answer: Data in use
cards.why: Data in use is being actively processed or held in memory by an application; in transit describes movement across a network, and at rest describes stored, inactive data.

cards.q: Under the US government classification system, exposure of certain military data would cause serious damage to national security. How should this data be classified?
cards.answer: Secret
cards.why: US classification maps expected damage to level: Confidential covers general damage, Secret covers serious damage, and Top Secret covers exceptionally grave damage to national security.

cards.q: An org keeps backups only as long as they're useful or legally required, then destroys them. This describes proper data ___.
cards.answer: retention
cards.why: Data retention governs how long information is kept: no longer than needed operationally or legally required, whichever is longer.

cards.q: Solvana Health shares a dataset with a contractor for software testing and strips out anything that could identify a patient. Which technique PRIMARILY achieves this?
cards.answer: Data de-identification
cards.why: De-identification is the umbrella technique for stripping identifying attributes before sharing; tokenization is one specific method, DLP only stops exfiltration, and declassification lowers an asset's overall label rather than scrubbing specific fields.

cards.q: Which of these does NOT belong in a data retention policy?
options: Which backup software or system is used
cards.answer: Which backup software or system is used
cards.why: Retention policy covers what, how long, and where data is kept; the specific backup system or media used to achieve that belongs in a backup policy, not the retention policy.

cards.q: Which factor is the MOST important indicator of a cloud provider's data security?
cards.answer: Encryption of data
cards.why: Encryption protects confidentiality even if other controls fail or unauthorized parties gain access; redundancy, cost, and physical security matter but don't by themselves protect the data's content.

cards.q: After a breach, management wants to know which assets mattered most. What measure reflects an asset's importance or worth to the org?
cards.answer: Asset value
cards.why: Asset value captures an asset's monetary and operational worth and sensitivity, letting the org prioritize protection; risk measures likelihood of compromise, and the other terms aren't standard valuation measures.

cards.q: Which of these does NOT reliably eliminate data remanence on a drive?
cards.answer: Formatting
cards.why: Formatting only rewrites the file system index, leaving most underlying data recoverable with basic tools; overwriting, shredding, and degaussing actually destroy or obscure the data itself.

cards.q: An org adds access logs to its backup servers to track which employees touch which datasets. This is an example of proper data ___.
cards.answer: handling
cards.why: Data handling covers who may access data and under what accountability; logging access is a handling control, not encryption, retention, or storage.

cards.q: Which of these does NOT reliably remove data remanence?
cards.answer: Deleting the files
cards.why: Deletion only removes the file system pointer; the underlying data remains recoverable until it's overwritten, degaussed, or the media is destroyed.

cards.q: Northwind Retail moves financial reports to a private cloud whose provider offers mutual certificate authentication and strong encryption. What level of protection should the reports receive?
options: Less, since the CSP already secures it
cards.answer: The same level as on-premises
cards.why: Protection requirements flow from the data's classification, not from where it's hosted; the CSP's extra features are welcome but don't change the baseline the classification policy mandates.

cards.q: Arcadia University outsources backup and storage to a managed security service provider. Who remains ULTIMATELY accountable for the data's security?
cards.answer: The data owner
cards.why: Outsourcing custody shifts operational tasks but not accountability; the data owner remains ultimately responsible regardless of where or by whom the data is processed.

cards.q: For disposing of old hard drives without leaving residual data behind, which method leaves no recovery tool able to bring the data back afterward?
options: Reinstalling the OS over the old one
cards.answer: Overwriting the drive
cards.why: Files can still be recovered after an OS reinstall, a format, or a simple deletion; a proper overwrite of multiple passes leaves no known recoverable remnant on functioning media.

cards.q: A department staffer skips IT provisioning and grabs a spare laptop from the supply closet for a new hire, prompting an asset-manager investigation. What TYPE of security violation is this?
cards.answer: Improper asset handling
cards.why: Issuing equipment outside authorized asset-management procedure is a handling violation, not theft since there was no malicious intent, and there's no indication of a marking or data-access failure.

cards.q: Which of these does NOT belong in a data retention policy?
options: How to restore safely from backup media
cards.answer: How to restore safely from backup media
cards.why: Restore procedures belong in a disaster-recovery plan or backup runbook; the retention policy only scopes what data is kept, for how long, and where.

cards.q: Which category of data poses the GREATEST privacy risk if it appears in network device log files?
cards.answer: Personal information
cards.why: Personal information can directly identify or locate an individual, creating the highest exposure risk for identity theft and privacy breach if it leaks through log files.

cards.q: When assigning a sensitivity label to data, which factor is LEAST relevant?
options: How the data will be used
cards.answer: How the data will be used
cards.why: Sensitivity reflects worth, exposure impact, and intended audience; the operational purpose the data is put to doesn't change how sensitive it is.

cards.q: A CEO keeps decommissioned computers because they still hold information the company needs, planning to dispose of them once that data is no longer required. Which element of asset retention is this?
cards.answer: Record retention
cards.why: Record retention is keeping information for as long as it remains useful before destruction; personnel retention concerns staff knowledge, media retention concerns preserving damaged media, and data corruption isn't a retention concept at all.

cards.q: Which practice best reflects a clean desk policy?
options: Shred all paper copies of everything
Pick up printouts immediately after printing
Use paper copies of sensitive data only while actively needed at the desk
cards.answer: Use paper copies of sensitive data only while actively needed at the desk
cards.why: A clean desk policy is about minimizing sensitive paper exposure, keeping sensitive printouts out unless actively in use, rather than general tidiness or a blanket shredding rule.

cards.q: Which of these questions is NOT something a data retention policy answers?
options: How should data be securely destroyed once retention expires?
How long must the data be kept?
Where is the physical backup infrastructure located?
cards.answer: Where is the physical backup infrastructure located?
cards.why: Retention policy scopes what data is kept, for how long, and how it's destroyed at end of life; the physical location of backup infrastructure is an operational storage or architecture decision, not a retention-policy question.

cards.q: A backup tape is stolen from a courier van. What control would prevent the data on it from being readable to the thief?
cards.answer: Proper data encryption
cards.why: Strong encryption renders the tape's contents unreadable without the key, protecting confidentiality even when the physical media itself is lost or stolen.

cards.q: What is the MOST fundamental purpose of an IT Asset Management (ITAM) program?
options: Maximize return on investment for IT assets
cards.answer: Maximize return on investment for IT assets
cards.why: ITAM tracks assets across their full lifecycle so the organization extracts maximum value from them; compliance, inventory accuracy, and access control are supporting outcomes, not the program's core purpose.

cards.q: An org has no degausser or disk shredder but must dispose of old hard drives securely. What is the BEST option?
options: Overwrite the working drives and ignore the damaged ones
Recycle them as e-waste since due care has been met
Dispose of them in a lake or the ocean
Pay a licensed third party to destroy them
cards.answer: Pay a licensed third party to destroy them
cards.why: Without in-house destruction capability, contracting a licensed destruction vendor bound by the org's security policy satisfies due diligence; ignoring damaged drives, recycling as-is, or illegal dumping all leave recoverable data exposed.

cards.q: Talus Mining has finalized an asset and data retention policy requiring all processors and controllers to follow it without exception. A team must now evaluate a requested exception. What should be the PRIMARY factor driving that decision?
cards.answer: Business requirements
cards.why: No exception can override binding legal or regulatory obligations, but within that boundary, whether an exception is granted ultimately turns on the business need driving the request; industry standards and internal frameworks are secondary inputs.

cards.q: A failed HDD in a high-availability cluster is swapped out by a third-party hardware vendor, who takes the damaged drive away for replacement. What's the potential issue?
options: Third-party vendors should never touch critical servers
The damaged drive's data remnants could be mishandled by the vendor
Health checks on the rest of the cluster won't run
There is no issue with this process
cards.answer: The damaged drive's data remnants could be mishandled by the vendor
cards.why: A failed drive can still hold recoverable data; unless it's sanitized per policy before it leaves custody, handing it to an outside vendor creates a data-remanence exposure even though the outage itself was handled smoothly.

cards.q: Vesper Aerospace handles PII, payroll, health data, and IP under a multi-tier classification scheme. How should it best handle data that is sensitive but doesn't fit its existing classified tiers?
options: Label everything unclassified as 'Sensitive' as a blanket default
Classify it all as 'Confidential' to be safe
Create a distinct 'Sensitive but Unclassified' tier with tailored protections
Label it 'Public' but keep minimal access controls
cards.answer: Create a distinct 'Sensitive but Unclassified' tier with tailored protections
cards.why: A dedicated tier lets the org apply protections proportional to actual risk for PII, PHI, and payroll data, avoiding both the under-protection of a blanket 'Public' label and the resource waste of over-protecting everything as 'Confidential.'

cards.q: Brightline Media receives a shipment of new servers for its network. What is the most critical action BEFORE integrating them into the infrastructure?
options: Update the asset tracking system with server details
Distribute servers to departments as needed
cards.answer: Harden each server's default configuration
cards.why: Vendor default configurations favor ease of use over security; hardening, disabling unneeded services, patching, and applying baselines must happen before a server is exposed to the network, ahead of distribution, inventory updates, or remote-wipe setup.

cards.q: A CSO suspects an employee is emailing confidential company data to a competitor. Which control BEST addresses this concern?
cards.answer: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) system
cards.why: DLP is purpose-built to detect and block sensitive data leaving the organization through channels like email; TLS only protects data in transit generically, IPS targets network attacks, and digital signatures address integrity and authenticity, not exfiltration.

cards.q: A decommissioned server holding sensitive data is donated to a charity after the data team runs only the OS's delete command. A charity insider later recovers data from it using forensic tools. What is the MOST probable root cause?
options: Data remanence left on the media
cards.answer: Data remanence left on the media
cards.why: OS-level delete commands only remove file-table pointers; without a stronger sanitization step such as overwrite, degauss, or physical destruction, remnant data stays recoverable, which is why media that held sensitive data shouldn't be donated even after being 'deleted.'

cards.q: An org purges data annually without archiving it. New regulation later demands a six-year audit trail it no longer has, triggering litigation. What would have PREVENTED this?
cards.answer: Asset retention policy
cards.why: A retention policy sets how long sensitive records must be kept before purging; without one, the org destroyed data it was later legally obligated to produce. Inventory and classification are prerequisites but don't by themselves dictate how long to keep records.

cards.q: A streaming platform's CISO wants to stop unauthorized content sharing. Which DRM strategy is the MOST comprehensive?
options: A multi-layered approach combining copy restrictions, persistent authentication, and audit trails
Persistent authentication alone requiring users to stay online
cards.answer: A multi-layered approach combining copy restrictions, persistent authentication, and audit trails
cards.why: Each single control has gaps: copy restrictions can be bypassed by screen recording, staying online alone doesn't stop screen sharing, and audit trails are purely reactive, so layering them gives both preventive and detective coverage.

cards.q: After classifying its data, an org layers a data categorization process on top. What is categorization's PRIMARY objective?
options: Apply consistent safeguards across data with similar sensitivity
Reduce risk to an acceptable level
Determine which security controls are needed
cards.answer: Apply consistent safeguards across data with similar sensitivity
cards.why: Categorization groups already-classified data by sensitivity so equivalent controls can be applied consistently; marking and labeling belongs to classification itself, risk reduction is risk management's job, and control selection follows from risk assessment.

cards.q: A publisher wants to stop unauthorized sharing of its e-books and identify who leaked a copy if one appears online. What is the MOST comprehensive approach?
options: Limit the number of devices that can access an e-book
A DRM system combining single-user licensing, tracking, and embedded metadata
Invisible metadata watermarking alone to trace leaks after the fact
A visible watermark showing the buyer's name
cards.answer: A DRM system combining single-user licensing, tracking, and embedded metadata
cards.why: Combining a license restriction with tracking and embedded metadata gives both preventive control by limiting access and reactive tracing by identifying the source; the other options each cover only deterrence, tracing, or device limits alone.

cards.q: A vulnerability assessment finds legacy systems running software whose end-of-support date is next month. What's the BIGGEST concern?
options: The software will simply stop running
Future vulnerabilities in it won't be patched by the vendor
New versions of the software won't be released
The vendor will stop selling that version
cards.answer: Future vulnerabilities in it won't be patched by the vendor
cards.why: End-of-support means the vendor stops issuing fixes, updates, and technical support, leaving any vulnerability discovered afterward permanently unpatched, which is the real security exposure since the software itself keeps running.

cards.q: A CSO wants a declassification control that replaces sensitive data values with non-sensitive substitute characters or numbers. Which control fits?
cards.answer: Tokenization
cards.why: Tokenization swaps a sensitive value for a non-sensitive token; masking obscures rather than substitutes with a distinct token, encryption relies on reversible keys rather than substitution, and steganography hides one message inside another.

cards.q: When implementing cloud reporting and compliance tooling, which factor is LEAST important?
options: Ease of use for end users
cards.answer: Ease of use for end users
cards.why: Compliance reporting is typically run by a specialized team trained to use less user-friendly tools, so usability matters far less here than the data's security, cost sustainability, and the platform's ability to scale with regulatory demand.

cards.q: An org centralizes its databases under one control system and needs an approach that keeps the data internally consistent long term. What is MOST effective for maintaining that integrity?
options: User-defined business rules triggered by user activity
Built-in DBMS features enforcing entity, referential, and semantic integrity
Automated change notifications sent after edits occur
cards.answer: Built-in DBMS features enforcing entity, referential, and semantic integrity
cards.why: Modern DBMS integrity features enforce rules automatically and proactively at the engine level; manual checks don't scale, notifications are only reactive, and user-defined rules cover specific triggered actions rather than integrity as a whole.

cards.q: After several breaches tied to poor data management, a company wants to improve security through database normalization. What's the MOST effective step?
options: Break the schema into function-specific tables to reduce redundancy
Merge records from several source systems into one wide table
cards.answer: Break the schema into function-specific tables to reduce redundancy
cards.why: Splitting the schema by function limits how much any single breach exposes and enables selective access rights per table; merging everything into one wide table increases blast radius, while removing duplicates or unneeded data improves quality but not structural security.

cards.q: A CISO wants a control that enforces confidentiality specifically for data on removable media that might be used without authorization. Which is BEST?
cards.answer: Full disk encryption (FDE)
cards.why: FDE protects the confidentiality of data sitting on the media itself, wherever it goes; hashing and digital signatures address integrity and authenticity rather than confidentiality, and IPSec only protects data while it's actively moving across a network.

cards.q: A company deploys a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB). Which practice does the MOST to raise its overall security level?
options: Implementing DLP policies to block unauthorized data exfiltration
Giving end users unrestricted access to all cloud apps
Disabling MFA for all users to simplify sign-in
cards.answer: Implementing DLP policies to block unauthorized data exfiltration
cards.why: DLP policies proactively stop sensitive data from leaving in the first place, complementing the CASB's visibility; log review alone is reactive, and unrestricted access or disabled MFA actively weaken security.

cards.q: After identifying assets and classifying data, what is the NEXT step toward selecting what to protect?
options: Configure controls based on secure practices
Use a security baseline to identify applicable controls
cards.answer: Use a security baseline to identify applicable controls
cards.why: A baseline such as ISO 27002 gives a starting control set for the classified assets; tailoring, scoping, and implementation are later steps that refine and deploy the baseline's chosen controls, not the immediate next step.

cards.q: Which of these is NOT true of BOTH data encryption and data masking?
options: Both can help meet compliance requirements
Both require a key to access the underlying data
Both protect data from unauthorized access
cards.answer: Both require a key to access the underlying data
cards.why: Encryption relies on a key for reversal, but masking permanently replaces values with realistic substitutes and has no key to reverse it; both, however, satisfy compliance requirements and restrict unauthorized access, so the key-based claim is the false generalization.

cards.q: After a breach, a security manager wants to implement database normalization to reduce risk. What is the MOST effective step?
options: Set up firewalls and access controls on the database
Use data mapping to find and eliminate redundant or inconsistent data
Create a separate database for each data type
cards.answer: Use data mapping to find and eliminate redundant or inconsistent data
cards.why: Normalization is fundamentally about restructuring data to remove redundancy and inconsistency, which data mapping identifies directly; firewalls, governance programs, and splitting into separate databases are valuable but don't perform normalization itself.

cards.q: A consultant's FDE-encrypted laptop is stolen; a week earlier he'd emailed his manager a personal, unapproved draft of research he'd been doing on his own initiative. The CISO must judge which concerns genuinely implicate the org's classification and labelling policy. Which of these is NOT a genuine risk under that policy?
options: Possible loss of the personal, not-yet-approved draft
Exposure of copyrighted material if the data is recovered
Assuming there's no risk purely because the laptop was encrypted
Ignoring the incident to protect the company's reputation
cards.answer: Possible loss of the personal, not-yet-approved draft
cards.why: A personal draft that was never adopted as an approved internal record falls outside the formal classification and labelling policy's scope, unlike genuine concerns such as assuming FDE alone guarantees safety, since it doesn't defend against all offline attacks, or suppressing disclosure to protect reputation, which erodes trust.

cards.q: A newly appointed department head objects to being named owner of the customer database, arguing the sysadmin team already handles its backups and patching. How should the security manager respond?
options: Ownership carries ultimate accountability for the asset's protection; day-to-day tasks can be delegated but accountability cannot
Ownership can be transferred to the sysadmin team since they perform the hands-on work
Ownership is only a formality with no bearing on protection decisions
Ownership should rotate quarterly between the department and IT to share the burden
cards.answer: Ownership carries ultimate accountability for the asset's protection; day-to-day tasks can be delegated but accountability cannot
cards.why: Assigning an owner is the key requirement for protection accountability: the owner, typically a senior manager or department head, remains organizationally accountable for ensuring appropriate controls exist even while delegating protection tasks to custodians and administrators.

cards.q: Reviewing the asset inventory before an acquisition, an analyst finds every server and laptop catalogued but no record of the company's patents, trademarks, or key software copyrights. What should she flag?
options: Intangible assets must also be inventoried and tracked so they can be protected
Nothing; inventories are only meant to cover physical hardware
Patents are protected by law for 20 years, so tracking them internally is redundant
Intellectual property belongs in the legal department's files, not the asset inventory
cards.answer: Intangible assets must also be inventoried and tracked so they can be protected
cards.why: Asset management covers both tangible assets (hardware, devices, documents) and intangible assets (patents, copyrights, trademarks, reputation); an organization cannot protect intellectual property it has not identified and tracked in its inventory.

cards.q: An operations lead is asked to justify the budget for a configuration management system plus RFID tagging of all hardware. What is the PRIMARY security goal this asset-management investment serves?
options: Preventing losses by tracking assets and protecting them throughout their lifetime
Speeding up help-desk ticket resolution times
Eliminating the need for physical security controls in the server room
Reducing the depreciation charges on the balance sheet
cards.answer: Preventing losses by tracking assets and protecting them throughout their lifetime
cards.why: The primary goal of asset management is loss prevention: an automated configuration management system and tracking tags (barcodes, RFID) let the organization know what hardware it has, where it is, and whether it is protected from inventory through disposal.

cards.q: A scan of workstations reveals dozens of applications installed beyond what the organization has purchased licenses for. Which provisioning practice addresses BOTH the legal exposure and the unapproved software?
options: Software asset management with license-compliance monitoring
Increasing the frequency of full-disk backups
cards.answer: Software asset management with license-compliance monitoring
cards.why: Managing software assets means monitoring license compliance to avoid legal issues and simultaneously ensuring systems do not run unauthorized software; the other options protect availability or confidentiality but do nothing about licensing or rogue installs.

cards.q: Meridian Bank is contracting outside testers to attack its trading platform. Who decides what the test is trying to achieve?
options: The outsourced testing firm's project lead
cards.answer: Senior management
cards.why: Senior management owns the risk being tested and must sign off on objectives before any engagement starts, since they answer for the outcome.

cards.q: A scoring rubric for rating vulnerability severity uses metrics such as Attack Vector, Attack Complexity, and Impact. Which term listed below is NOT one of its metrics?
cards.answer: Durability
cards.why: CVSS scores vulnerabilities using vectors like attack vector, complexity, privileges, and CIA impact categories; 'durability' is not part of that vocabulary.

cards.q: An examiner checks whether existing safeguards protecting a payroll application are actually reducing risk as intended. What is this examiner performing?
cards.answer: A Security Control Assessment (SCA)
cards.why: An SCA specifically tests implemented controls to confirm they work as designed and are meeting the organization's protection goals.

cards.q: Nimbus Retail traces a breach to a cross-site scripting flaw with a base severity score of 6.4 on a 0-10 scale. How should this be classified?
cards.answer: Medium
cards.why: Under the standard 0.1-10.0 severity bands, scores from roughly 4.0 to 6.9 fall in the Medium range, below the High and Critical thresholds.

cards.q: Before paying for a formal, standards-based audit, a firm wants an 'informal' review first. What does that typically involve?
options: In-house staff looking for weaknesses on their own
Employees double-checking their own daily work
Comparing controls against a published certification standard
Bringing in a licensed external audit firm
cards.answer: In-house staff looking for weaknesses on their own
cards.why: An informal, unstructured review is usually internal staff hunting for gaps ahead of time, without being measured against a formal published standard.

cards.q: A penetration test scoping document sets IP ranges, time windows, and rules of engagement. What would it NOT contain?
cards.answer: Employees' full medical records
cards.why: A pentest statement of work defines scope, timing, and engagement rules; unrelated protected health data has no place in it and would create needless liability.

cards.q: When an organization begins a formal data-collection effort, what should happen first?
options: Define the scope and objectives of what will be collected
Pick the tools that will gather the data
Analyze whatever data has come in
cards.answer: Define the scope and objectives of what will be collected
cards.why: Scoping comes first because it determines what tools, sources, and analysis methods are even relevant to the collection effort.

cards.q: What is the most effective way to run a credentialed vulnerability scan?
options: Skip credentials entirely and scan externally
Use one account shared across multiple scanning tools
Hardcode credentials into the scanner at installation
Have the system administrator issue the scanner its own dedicated, least-privilege credentials
cards.answer: Have the system administrator issue the scanner its own dedicated, least-privilege credentials
cards.why: Purpose-issued, minimally privileged credentials from the administrator let the scanner see authenticated-only findings while limiting damage if those credentials leak.

cards.q: A vulnerability scan flags several findings as LOW severity. What does that rating most likely mean?
options: The systems have no vulnerabilities at all
The flaw exists but is not exploitable, or exploiting it has negligible impact
Low findings are noise and can be deleted unread
The flaw is exploitable and its impact would be severe
cards.answer: The flaw exists but is not exploitable, or exploiting it has negligible impact
cards.why: A LOW rating still reflects a real finding; it simply means the exploit path or resulting impact is minimal, so it still warrants review even if not urgent action.

cards.q: A staff member is picking audit frameworks for use across all of a company's branch offices. Which framework would they be unlikely to recommend?
cards.answer: ITIL
cards.why: ITIL is a service-management practice framework, not an audit standard, whereas ISO/IEC 27002, COBIT, and SSAE-based attestations are all built for audit use.

cards.q: Which of these would generally fall outside the scope of a routine security assessment?
options: The organization's security policies and procedures
The physical security of company facilities
cards.answer: Employees' personal social media posts
cards.why: Personal social media activity sits outside the technical, administrative, and physical controls a standard assessment examines, and reviewing it raises privacy concerns.

cards.q: What is the most effective way to gather ongoing data about how well security processes are operating?
options: Build automated collection into a security management platform
Have employees self-report what they did
Survey staff about their understanding of procedures
Wait for the next scheduled audit
cards.answer: Build automated collection into a security management platform
cards.why: Automated collection is continuous and objective, capturing detail like breach attempts and permission changes that manual self-reporting or periodic surveys would miss.

cards.q: What do vulnerability scans most commonly turn up?
options: Open ports that shouldn't be open
cards.answer: Open ports that shouldn't be open
cards.why: Scanners are built to flag common misconfigurations like unnecessary open ports, outdated software, and missing patches, not live attacks.

cards.q: A high-severity flaw was just found in a production application. What is the correct way to assign it a severity score?
options: Calculate it using the standard published scoring formula
