cards.why: SDN pulls the control plane, the logic that decides how traffic should flow, out of individual switches and into a centralized controller, leaving the data plane in the hardware to simply forward packets as instructed; SDDC virtualizes an entire data center's infrastructure, NFV replaces dedicated appliances with virtualized network functions, and a CDN caches and distributes content rather than centralizing routing control.

cards.q: When implementing IPsec, which of the following is NOT inherently part of the protocol suite?
cards.answer: Network Address Translation
cards.why: IPsec provides authentication, encryption, and key management as core components, but NAT is a separate addressing function and can actually conflict with IPsec's integrity checks unless NAT traversal is added.

cards.q: A CISO's team detects unusual activity traced to a war-dialing attempt against legacy dial-up modems still supporting critical applications. What should be the PRIMARY course of action?
options: Roll out security awareness training focused on war dialing
Put the dial-up lines under close, continuous monitoring paired with tightened access restrictions
Deploy more advanced network IDS/IPS across the environment
Immediately replace all dial-up modems and retire the legacy systems
cards.answer: Put the dial-up lines under close, continuous monitoring paired with tightened access restrictions
cards.why: Monitoring the dial-up lines and tightening access controls directly addresses the exposure without the operational disruption of ripping out systems the business still depends on; network IDS/IPS is built for digital intrusions and won't catch analog dial-up attacks, and training doesn't address a modem-based vector.

cards.q: An enterprise needs to separate its most critical internal systems from its public-facing services using a firewall deployment architecture. Which architecture provides the MOST security?
cards.answer: Screened subnet
cards.why: A screened subnet (DMZ) uses two packet-filtering routers plus a bastion host to create layered defense between the internet, the DMZ, and the internal network, offering more protection than a single dual-homed firewall, a screened host, or a bastion host alone.

cards.q: Finance staff have been responding to fraudulent invoices sent from spoofed domains. The CFO wants a low-cost technical control that won't disrupt legitimate client correspondence. What control BEST addresses this?
cards.answer: Sender Policy Framework (SPF)
cards.why: SPF lets a domain publish which mail servers are authorized to send on its behalf, letting receiving systems reject or flag spoofed messages, without the key-management burden that PGP or S/MIME would add.

cards.q: Which statement about circuit-level firewalls is FALSE?
options: They operate at layer 5, the session layer, of the OSI model
They perform deep packet inspection of application content
SOCKS is a common circuit-level firewall implementation
cards.answer: They perform deep packet inspection of application content
cards.why: Circuit-level firewalls only validate the session handshake and track connection state at layer 5; they do not inspect application payload content, which is what distinguishes them from application-layer firewalls.

cards.q: A CISO is weighing whether to migrate legacy telephony to VoIP. Considering strategic and security tradeoffs together, what is the MOST compelling reason to make the switch?
options: VoIP works across wireless and satellite links
VoIP is significantly more cost-effective than traditional analog telephony
VoIP can run on any internet-connected device
cards.answer: VoIP is significantly more cost-effective than traditional analog telephony
cards.why: Reusing existing IP infrastructure for voice cuts the cost of running separate voice and data networks, which is usually the decisive business driver even though multimedia features, device flexibility, and network-agnosticism are real secondary benefits.

cards.q: A network administrator backs up firewall configurations nightly from regional offices worldwide over TFTP. An audit flags this as insecure. Which redesign gives the strongest, most privacy-preserving end-to-end protection for those backups?
options: Connect the offices with a virtual circuit over frame relay
Use a host-to-host IPsec tunnel to the TFTP server
Switch to SFTP instead of TFTP
Tunnel TFTP traffic over per-server SSH connections
cards.answer: Use a host-to-host IPsec tunnel to the TFTP server
cards.why: A host-to-host IPsec tunnel encrypts and hides the traffic end-to-end without exposing header metadata to analysis, while frame relay alone provides no encryption, plain SFTP still leaks header and traffic patterns, and managing per-server SSH key pairs creates a key-management burden.

cards.q: Using NAT overload (PAT), how many public IP addresses are required for 7 private hosts that all need simultaneous internet access?
cards.why: PAT, or NAT overload, maps many private hosts to one public IP by distinguishing sessions with unique source ports, so a single public address can serve all of them simultaneously.

cards.q: A multinational's full-mesh router network uses both IGP and BGP. Router failure risk threatens convergence and route availability as the company grows. What is the PRIMARY strategy to mitigate this risk?
options: Regularly back up configurations and maintain static routes for manual failover
Shift more routing responsibility onto BGP and reduce IGP use
Deploy redundant routers with dynamic routing protocols that support fast rerouting
Add monitoring tools to alert the team when a router fails
cards.answer: Deploy redundant routers with dynamic routing protocols that support fast rerouting
cards.why: Redundant routers combined with dynamic routing protocols that reconverge quickly keep the network resilient automatically, whereas manual static-route failover is slow, monitoring alone only detects rather than prevents impact, and BGP is designed for exterior, not fast interior, convergence.

cards.q: During an incident review of server 10.4.4.25, you check its firewall rule set, evaluated top to bottom, to see which rule set correctly blocks web access to the server. Which rule set actually denies both HTTP and HTTPS access?
options: DENY IP 10.4.4.25 80 then PERMIT IP ANY ANY
PERMIT IP ANY ANY then DENY IP 10.4.4.25 21
DENY IP 10.4.4.25 443 then PERMIT IP ANY ANY
DENY IP 10.4.4.25 443, DENY IP 10.4.4.25 80, then PERMIT IP ANY ANY
cards.answer: DENY IP 10.4.4.25 443, DENY IP 10.4.4.25 80, then PERMIT IP ANY ANY
cards.why: Firewall rules are evaluated in order, so both the HTTP port 80 and HTTPS port 443 deny statements must precede the catch-all permit; the other rule sets leave one of the two web ports open or place the permit-all rule before any explicit deny.

cards.q: A homeowner's smart thermostat pairs to a phone over Bluetooth with a 4-digit PIN. He notices the house heats up overnight without anyone touching a control and suspects remote interference. What type of attack is most likely occurring?
cards.answer: Bluebugging
cards.why: Bluebugging lets an attacker pair with a device and create a backdoor for ongoing remote control, matching repeated unauthorized setting changes; bluejacking only sends unsolicited messages, bluesnarfing steals data rather than controlling functions, and bluesmacking is a denial-of-service attack.

cards.q: Employees keep plugging unauthorized wireless access points into weak-coverage areas of the office LAN. As part of a broader strategy, what technical control on the switches would MOST directly stop this?
options: Opening every port on the switches
Enabling port security to restrict which devices can connect
cards.answer: Enabling port security to restrict which devices can connect
cards.why: Port security, limiting or locking down which devices may connect to a switch port, directly blocks unauthorized devices like rogue access points, while SSID hiding or rotation only obscures the legitimate network and doesn't stop rogue hardware being plugged in.

cards.q: A cafe owner inside a shopping mall wants her free guest Wi-Fi signal to stay confined to her shop so neighboring tenants and their customers can't access or attack it. Which technology achieves this?
options: Isolating the guest network with a VLAN
Installing a Faraday cage around the shop
cards.answer: Installing a Faraday cage around the shop
cards.why: A Faraday cage physically blocks RF signals from propagating beyond its enclosure, containing the Wi-Fi signal to the shop; a VLAN or captive portal only add logical segmentation or authentication and don't stop the RF from reaching neighboring units, and an air gap disconnects a network entirely rather than shaping signal propagation.

cards.q: Which approach is the MOST effective way to implement Network Access Control across a mixed environment of managed, unmanaged, and IoT devices?
options: User authentication plus access control lists
A dedicated NAC appliance performing posture and identity checks before granting access
cards.answer: A dedicated NAC appliance performing posture and identity checks before granting access
cards.why: A dedicated NAC appliance evaluates device health, identity, and connection context holistically before admitting a device to the network, whereas firewalls filter traffic post-connection and RBAC or ACLs govern resource access rather than network admission itself.

cards.q: A cloud provider's network currently tops out at 4,094 VLAN segments but needs to support up to 16 million logical segments for tenant isolation. Which technology BEST provides this scale?
cards.answer: Virtual eXtensible LAN (VXLAN)
cards.why: VXLAN's 24-bit segment ID supports roughly 16 million logical networks, far beyond the 12-bit, 4,094-segment VLAN limit, by tunneling layer-2 segments over a layer-3 underlay.

cards.q: Which of these is the MOST effective way to defend a public-facing server against a SYN flood attack?
options: Enabling SYN cookies so the server doesn't allocate state for unacknowledged connections
Deploying a network intrusion detection system
cards.answer: Enabling SYN cookies so the server doesn't allocate state for unacknowledged connections
cards.why: SYN cookies let the server encode connection state into the SYN-ACK itself rather than reserving resources up front, so half-open connections from the flood can't exhaust its connection table; a NIDS only detects the attack, disabling TCP timestamps addresses a different issue, and a basic firewall generally can't distinguish spoofed SYNs from legitimate ones.

cards.q: An employee's rogue access point was compromised and led to a breach exposing thousands of customer records. Aside from awareness training, what technical control could have prevented this?
options: Administratively shutting down unused switch ports
cards.answer: Administratively shutting down unused switch ports
cards.why: Shutting down unused switch ports prevents any unauthorized device, including a rogue access point, from ever getting network connectivity in the first place; SSID hiding, patching, and periodic scans don't stop a device from physically plugging into an open port.

cards.q: An IT manager is briefing the team on adding client-side certificate authentication to the company's internal web servers under TLS. Which statement best characterizes this feature and its use?
options: It's a commonly used, mandatory feature that always authenticates both client and server
It's an outdated feature that adds little value since only the server needs authenticating
It's rarely useful because servers don't typically need to authenticate the client
It's a selectively used feature, applied when heightened assurance is needed that only authorized individuals reach the server
cards.answer: It's a selectively used feature, applied when heightened assurance is needed that only authorized individuals reach the server
cards.why: Client-side TLS authentication via certificates adds mutual assurance and is deployed deliberately in high-sensitivity scenarios rather than by default, since it adds certificate-management overhead most deployments don't require.

cards.q: A CISO is evaluating Li-Fi as a supplement to existing Wi-Fi in select high-security office spaces to boost data transmission speed. Weighing range, reliability, and cost concerns, what should be the PRIMARY consideration driving the decision?
options: Li-Fi's short range may limit practicality in large offices
The current high cost of Li-Fi implementation relative to expected future price drops
Li-Fi's reliability varies with line-of-sight and environmental conditions
The need for compatibility between Li-Fi hardware and software and existing infrastructure
cards.answer: The current high cost of Li-Fi implementation relative to expected future price drops
cards.why: Cost is the dominant near-term factor shaping budget and ROI decisions for a large-scale Li-Fi rollout today, even though range, line-of-sight reliability, and infrastructure compatibility are all real secondary concerns that a phased or hybrid deployment could offset.

cards.q: Full-scale DR simulation is too risky for live operations. What lower-risk test format still validates the plan?
options: Tabletop exercise walking the team through the plan
Full interruption test on production systems
Unannounced live failover of the primary data center
Skipping testing until the next disaster occurs
cards.answer: Tabletop exercise walking the team through the plan
cards.why: A tabletop exercise discusses the plan step by step without touching production, giving assurance without the operational risk of a live drill.

cards.q: What is the PRIMARY reason an enterprise SOC builds out centralized logging and monitoring?
options: To detect and stop security breaches as they happen
To satisfy an annual compliance checklist
To help the helpdesk debug printer issues
To generate usage statistics for management reports
cards.answer: To detect and stop security breaches as they happen
cards.why: Logging and monitoring exist first and foremost to give the organization real-time visibility so it can detect and respond to breaches; compliance and troubleshooting are secondary benefits.

cards.q: Which approach BEST implements dual control over approval of access to a sensitive payroll database?
options: Two separate people must independently review and approve each request
One approver handles requests and a second person spot-checks 5 percent later
One approver processes requests with no second reviewer
One approver processes requests and a peer audits all of them a month later
cards.answer: Two separate people must independently review and approve each request
cards.why: True dual control requires two independent people to concur before the action takes effect, not after-the-fact sampling or unilateral approval.

cards.q: During a building emergency, whose safety must be secured FIRST?
options: Employees and other people on site
The physical structure of the building
cards.answer: Employees and other people on site
cards.why: Personnel safety always takes priority over protecting equipment, records, or property during an emergency.

cards.q: An organization wants automated detection AND automated response coordinated across its whole environment, not just alerting. Which tool category BEST fits?
options: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) alone
cards.answer: Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR)
cards.why: SOAR platforms orchestrate playbooks across many tools to both detect and automatically respond to incidents, going beyond the alerting-only scope of a SIEM, IPS, or EDR in isolation.

cards.q: Why might a backup administrator choose daily incremental backups over daily differential backups?
options: Incremental backups complete faster because each one only captures data changed since the last backup
Incremental backups make restores faster than differentials
Incremental backups let you exclude specific directories, which differentials cannot do
Incremental backups always capture the full data set every night
cards.answer: Incremental backups complete faster because each one only captures data changed since the last backup
cards.why: Incremental backups reset the archive bit each run, so each incremental only covers changes since the prior incremental, making backup windows shorter than differentials — at the cost of a more complex restore.

cards.q: Which BCP subplan governs how the organization talks to the press and keeps employees informed during a disaster?
cards.answer: Crisis Communications Plan
cards.why: The Crisis Communications Plan defines who is authorized to speak to media and how internal and external stakeholders are kept informed during a disaster.

cards.q: A planning team wants a recovery site that can restore critical applications within roughly an hour of a declared disaster. Which site type fits?
options: Mobile site with no pre-installed equipment
Reciprocal agreement site with no dedicated hardware
cards.answer: Hot site
cards.why: A hot site keeps critical systems on standby, often pre-configured though at lower capacity than the primary, so failover can typically be completed within about an hour.

cards.q: IT is building a standard workstation image that disables every service, port, and feature not strictly needed for daily work. This configuration principle is called ___.
cards.answer: Least functionality
cards.why: Least functionality is the principle of building systems with only the minimum services, ports, and protocols enabled; least privilege instead governs the access rights a user or process holds.

cards.q: Which process governs applying vendor software updates to systems on a recurring monthly schedule?
cards.answer: Patch management
cards.why: Patch management is the recurring cycle of identifying, testing, and deploying vendor-released fixes, such as a monthly patch cycle, to keep software current and secure.

cards.q: Which of these is NOT a legitimate step in a change management review and approval process?
options: Implementing the change before it is reviewed or approved
Assessing the change's impact on the organization
cards.answer: Implementing the change before it is reviewed or approved
cards.why: Change management exists precisely to prevent unreviewed changes from reaching production; skipping review and approval defeats the process rather than being a step within it.

cards.q: For visual inspection of magnetic-stripe ID badges, which feature is hardest for an attacker to forge?
options: The cardholder's printed name and department
Printed health information on the card
cards.answer: An embedded hologram
cards.why: Embedded holograms require specialized equipment to reproduce, making them far harder to counterfeit than a printed photo or text field during a quick visual check.

cards.q: Who is legally permitted to act under exigent circumstances (an immediate threat to life or evidence)?
cards.answer: Law enforcement officers
cards.why: Exigent-circumstances authority to bypass normal warrant procedures applies only to law enforcement, or those acting under color of law, when there is an immediate threat to life or risk of evidence destruction.

cards.q: Which power configuration provides TRUE redundancy for a server's dual power supplies?
options: Each power supply connected to a separate, independent UPS
Both power supplies connected to the same UPS
A single power supply with no UPS
Two power supplies with only one cabled in at a time, manually swapped on failure
cards.answer: Each power supply connected to a separate, independent UPS
cards.why: Genuine redundancy requires eliminating single points of failure, so each power supply must feed from a distinct UPS rather than sharing one upstream source.

cards.q: A team restricts network communication to only the IP addresses, ports, and protocols explicitly authorized by leadership, denying everything else by default. What is this practice called?
cards.answer: Allowlisting
cards.why: Allowlisting permits only pre-approved communications and denies everything else by default, which is the opposite of blocklisting's deny-specific-items approach.

cards.q: A DR exercise reveals outdated recovery procedures. What should happen immediately AFTER the exercise to address this?
options: Document lessons learned and update the DR plan
Restart the same exercise from the beginning
Immediately run a full Business Continuity Plan test
Exercise the crisis communications plan instead
cards.answer: Document lessons learned and update the DR plan
cards.why: Post-exercise activity should capture lessons learned and feed corrections back into the DR plan so the gaps found in testing are actually closed.

cards.q: A junior analyst responding to a suspected malware incident finds a frozen desktop and reboots it before imaging the system. Which forensic requirement did this violate?
options: Preserving and isolating system state before analysis
Having a certified expert perform the analysis
cards.answer: Preserving and isolating system state before analysis
cards.why: Rebooting a live system before it is imaged or isolated destroys volatile evidence, violating the requirement to preserve system state as the first step of a forensic response.

cards.q: A company moves into a large multi-story building and must update evacuation procedures. What should be the top priority?
options: Designating a responsible person for evacuating each floor
Buying the most advanced notification system regardless of cost
Requiring every employee to memorize the plan verbatim
Assigning one senior manager to run the whole building's evacuation alone
cards.answer: Designating a responsible person for evacuating each floor
cards.why: A large multi-story building needs distributed accountability, so assigning a floor warden per floor scales evacuation coordination better than relying on a single point of responsibility.

cards.q: A CISO works alongside the incident response coordinator through BCP/DR planning, drills, and eventual real disasters. Which personal ability matters MOST when a disaster actually strikes?
options: The ability to cope with stress and remain composed under pressure
Being the one who single-handedly wrote the BCP/DRP
Personally assessing the severity of every disaster alone
Working closely with stakeholders during the planning phase only
cards.answer: The ability to cope with stress and remain composed under pressure
cards.why: Because real disasters are high-pressure events, the ability to stay composed and follow procedure under stress is what keeps a response effective, more than planning-phase skills alone.

cards.q: Which of these is not typically a pitfall in audit log management?
options: Consolidating log collection onto one hardened, access-controlled server
Logs are not retained long enough
Logs are not standardized or viewable in a SIEM
Logs are not reviewed on a timely, regular basis
cards.answer: Consolidating log collection onto one hardened, access-controlled server
cards.why: Centralizing collection onto a protected server is a best practice, not a pitfall; the common problems are inadequate retention, lack of standardization/SIEM visibility, and infrequent review.

cards.q: Facing widespread misconfigurations and outdated components across a mixed legacy/cloud stack, what should a CISO prioritize as the primary fix?
options: Systematic hardening and patch management across all systems
Regular penetration testing and threat modeling alone
An extensive risk analysis before touching any configuration
cards.answer: Systematic hardening and patch management across all systems
cards.why: Hardening and patch management directly remediate the root causes — misconfigurations and unpatched, outdated components — while testing and training are valuable but do not by themselves fix the exposures.

cards.q: A zero-downtime-tolerant company wants an annual DRP exercise that is minimally intrusive yet gives strong assurance the plan works. Which test type fits BEST?
cards.answer: Simulation testing
cards.why: Simulation testing exercises the plan against a scripted scenario without disrupting live operations, offering more assurance than a walkthrough while avoiding the risk of a full interruption or parallel test.

cards.q: A critical server's actual recovery time has been exceeding its Maximum Tolerable Downtime. Which approach BEST reduces the Recovery Time Objective?
options: Implementing high availability with active replication
Switching to differential backups instead of incremental
Switching to incremental backups instead of differential
Extending the MTD to match current recovery capability
cards.answer: Implementing high availability with active replication
cards.why: High availability architectures with active replication let a standby take over almost immediately, directly shrinking recovery time compared with backup-based restore approaches.

cards.q: After a hardened server baseline goes into production, ongoing monitoring for baseline drift primarily serves what purpose?
options: Ensuring no unauthorized change weakens the security posture
Measuring server speed and uptime performance
Establishing what normal behavior looks like for later reference
cards.answer: Ensuring no unauthorized change weakens the security posture
cards.why: Baseline drift monitoring exists to catch unauthorized configuration changes that could erode the hardening applied at deployment, not primarily to track performance or normal-behavior baselining.

cards.q: Sensitive printouts routinely sit unattended at a shared printer. Which control addresses this with the LEAST workflow disruption?
options: Secure print-release software requiring authentication at the printer
A total ban on printing sensitive data
CCTV cameras trained on every printer
A policy restricting printing to designated personnel
cards.answer: Secure print-release software requiring authentication at the printer
cards.why: Pull-printing requires the sender to authenticate at the device before output is released, closing the exposure window without banning printing or adding heavy procedural overhead.

cards.q: As headcount and departments grow, tracking access permissions manually is becoming unmanageable. What is the best course of action?
options: Deploy automated tools to monitor and manage access and security controls
Hire additional IT security staff to handle the manual workload
Add more security protocols on top of the existing manual process
Simplify org structure to reduce the number of departments
cards.answer: Deploy automated tools to monitor and manage access and security controls
cards.why: Automated security and access-management tooling scales with organizational complexity far better than adding manual headcount or layering on more manual controls.

cards.q: A technician opens a firewall port to fix a complaint without documenting or approving the change; an attacker later abuses that port. Which process should have been followed?
cards.answer: Change management
cards.why: Any modification to a production control, such as opening a port, should go through change management so the risk is evaluated and approved before implementation, not applied ad hoc.

cards.q: After a malware incident, the team's root-cause analysis work to determine why the attack succeeded happens MAINLY in which incident management phase?
cards.answer: Remediation
cards.why: Root cause analysis is core remediation work: identifying why the incident occurred so the underlying weakness is fixed, distinct from containment (response) or restoring service (recovery).

cards.q: An attacker splits malicious traffic into many small packet fragments to slip past an IPS signature match. What technique is this?
options: Using a well-known port to blend in with normal traffic
Coordinating many source IPs at low bandwidth
cards.answer: Fragmentation to evade signature detection
cards.why: Breaking traffic into fragments prevents the IPS from reassembling and matching the full attack pattern against its signatures, letting the payload slip through undetected.

cards.q: What is the FIRST step when standing up a warm-site disaster recovery capability?
options: Inventorying and ranking which business functions and applications matter most
Signing a contract with a warm-site vendor
Installing physical infrastructure at the warm site
Writing and testing the disaster recovery plan
cards.answer: Inventorying and ranking which business functions and applications matter most
cards.why: Recovery planning must start by identifying what actually needs to be recovered and its priority, before selecting a site, contracting a vendor, or building infrastructure.

cards.q: A data center's FM200 system keeps triggering because dust accumulates under the raised floor. What is the most effective fix?
options: Put a recurring cleaning cadence in place for the raised-floor void
Add more ventilation fans below the floor
cards.answer: Put a recurring cleaning cadence in place for the raised-floor void
cards.why: Regular cleaning underneath the raised floor removes the root cause — accumulated dust — rather than just masking the symptom by desensitizing the detector or altering environmental conditions.

cards.q: To preserve evidence integrity on a compromised hard drive, what should the investigator do?
options: Hash the original drive, make a bit-level copy, verify matching hashes, and analyze only the copy
Encrypt the original drive and analyze it directly
Copy visible files to a new drive and analyze the new drive
Pull the drive, reformat it, and reinstall it elsewhere
cards.answer: Hash the original drive, make a bit-level copy, verify matching hashes, and analyze only the copy
cards.why: Hashing the source before and after imaging, and analyzing only a verified bit-for-bit copy, proves the original was never altered and preserves the evidentiary chain.

cards.q: Which logging architecture BEST preserves audit log integrity if the source system is actively compromised?
options: Real-time log shipping over a one-way (simplex) link to an isolated central server
Local logs accessible only to administrators
Local logs pushed to a central server every 24 hours
Central log collection that pulls new entries once an hour
cards.answer: Real-time log shipping over a one-way (simplex) link to an isolated central server
cards.why: A one-way real-time feed to a separate segment means an attacker on the compromised host has no path back to alter or delete logs already shipped, unlike periodic pushes or locally stored logs.

cards.q: A vulnerability scan flags Log4j findings on five servers. Following the standard vulnerability management workflow, what is the NEXT step?
options: Validate whether the servers are actually vulnerable
Begin patching all five servers immediately
cards.answer: Validate whether the servers are actually vulnerable
cards.why: The standard workflow is detect, validate, remediate; after detection the team must confirm the finding is a true positive before committing to patching or escalating to incident response.

cards.q: Which activity best characterizes a genuine full interruption test of a disaster recovery plan?
options: Actually invoking backups and DR systems while production is shut down
Running a simulated cyberattack scenario on paper
Conducting a penetration test against live systems
Briefly powering off systems with no recovery activity
cards.answer: Actually invoking backups and DR systems while production is shut down
cards.why: A full interruption test halts primary operations and actually exercises backups and recovery systems to prove they can restore service, unlike a tabletop or simulation that avoids real disruption.

cards.q: Full backups run every Sunday at midnight; incrementals run every other night at midnight. The system fails Wednesday afternoon. How many tapes are needed to restore?
options: 3 (Sunday full plus Monday and Tuesday incrementals)
4 (Sunday full plus Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday incrementals)
cards.answer: 3 (Sunday full plus Monday and Tuesday incrementals)
cards.why: Restoring with incrementals requires the last full backup plus every incremental since then in order — here the Sunday full and the Monday and Tuesday night incrementals, three tapes total.

cards.q: When implementing an application allowlist, which measure is MOST important for verifying that only genuine, unaltered software runs?
options: Requiring each approved application to carry a trusted digital certificate and known hash
Letting users freely download anything from official vendor sites if it is on the list
Confirming allowlisted apps are compatible with other installed software
Refreshing the allowlist regularly as business needs change
cards.answer: Requiring each approved application to carry a trusted digital certificate and known hash
cards.why: A certificate and known hash verify that the executable is authentic and unmodified, which is the core security guarantee an allowlist is meant to provide beyond simply naming approved titles.

cards.q: Before releasing a new in-house application, the security team runs it on an isolated test network specifically to check whether the changes introduced new vulnerabilities. What change management activity is this?
cards.answer: Security Impact Analysis
cards.why: Security Impact Analysis is the change management activity where security specifically evaluates whether a proposed change introduces new vulnerabilities or compliance issues before release.

cards.q: In the incident management lifecycle, which sequence correctly lists the LAST three phases in order?
cards.answer: Recovery, remediation, lessons learned
cards.why: The lifecycle closes with recovery (restoring operations), remediation (fixing the root cause), and lessons learned (capturing improvements) in that order.

cards.q: An attacker spreads a scan across many coordinated low-bandwidth agents, each using different source IPs and ports, to avoid triggering IPS thresholds. What is this technique?
options: Low-and-slow coordinated attack distribution across multiple agents
Fragmenting packets to break up the attack signature
Using a well-known port to disguise malicious traffic
cards.answer: Low-and-slow coordinated attack distribution across multiple agents
cards.why: Spreading activity across many agents and source IPs at low volume makes it hard for the IPS to correlate the individual packets and recognize the coordinated scan.

cards.q: When measuring the success of a disaster recovery restoration, which indicator matters MOST?
options: Compliance with the defined RTO and RPO
Total cost of the restoration effort
Subjective quality of the restored systems
Raw wall-clock time to restore systems
cards.answer: Compliance with the defined RTO and RPO
cards.why: RTO and RPO are the pre-agreed targets for how quickly and how completely data must be restored, making compliance with them the key success measure rather than cost or unmeasured time alone.

cards.q: When designing access control for a new sensitive data center, which approach best reflects defense in depth?
options: A blended mix of administrative, technical, and physical controls with ongoing training
Physical controls only, such as locked cabinets and secure doors
Technical controls only, such as biometrics and smart cards
Administrative controls only, via policy and training
cards.answer: A blended mix of administrative, technical, and physical controls with ongoing training
cards.why: Defense in depth layers administrative, technical, and physical controls together, reinforced by continuous awareness training, rather than relying on any single control category.

cards.q: After several breaches, an investigator gathers and analyzes data from multiple sources to identify how the intrusions occurred. What is this process called?
cards.answer: Evidence collection
cards.why: Evidence collection, also called artifact gathering, is the systematic process of obtaining and analyzing information to identify how a breach or vulnerability occurred.

cards.q: Which of the following is the MOST reliable indicator of a system's current security posture?
options: The system has no known unpatched vulnerabilities
The system has never been attacked before
The system was patched at some point recently
The system has a written security policy on file
cards.answer: The system has no known unpatched vulnerabilities
cards.why: The absence of known, exploitable vulnerabilities is a direct, verifiable measure of exposure, unlike a clean attack history, a stale patch date, or a policy document that says nothing about actual state.

cards.q: Which outcome best signals that a full interruption drill of the DR plan actually succeeded?
options: The organization was able to recover operations from the interruption
The interruption lasted the longest possible duration
The interruption caused a complete system crash
The interruption resulted in zero data loss regardless of recovery
cards.answer: The organization was able to recover operations from the interruption
cards.why: The point of a full interruption test is to prove recovery actually works; successful recovery from the deliberate outage is the defining measure of success, not the duration or severity of the outage itself.

cards.q: A healthcare CISO must design recovery strategies spanning cold/warm/hot sites and cloud SaaS applications. What is the best overall approach?
options: Base recovery strategy on system criticality, weighing feasible options against cost and time
Base recovery strategy purely on potential financial impact, ignoring criticality
Focus recovery planning only on the highest tier systems and skip the rest
Apply every possible recovery option uniformly to every system
cards.answer: Base recovery strategy on system criticality, weighing feasible options against cost and time
cards.why: Effective recovery planning tiers investment to system criticality and balances it against cost and recovery-time feasibility, rather than fixating on cost alone or applying one blanket strategy everywhere.

cards.q: Which control category example is BOTH a technical control and a directive control?
cards.answer: Configuration standards
cards.why: Configuration standards direct how systems must be technically set up, functioning simultaneously as a directive instruction and a technical control, unlike job rotation (administrative/detective) or a policy document (purely administrative).

cards.q: A change control workflow includes these six activities in some order: file the RFC, assess impact, review, build, test, implement. What is the correct sequence?
options: Submission -> Assess -> Review -> Build -> Test -> Implement
Submission -> Review -> Assess -> Build -> Test -> Implement
Submission -> Assess -> Review -> Build -> Implement -> Test
Submission -> Assess -> Build -> Review -> Test -> Implement
cards.answer: Submission -> Assess -> Review -> Build -> Test -> Implement
cards.why: A standard change control flow submits the RFC, assesses its impact, has it reviewed for approval, then builds, tests, and finally implements the change in production.

cards.q: Immediately after discovering a data breach on a complex, multi-server network, what is the most important first action for the response team?
options: Contain the incident by pulling impacted hosts off the network
Conduct a full forensic analysis before taking any other action
Notify all employees and stakeholders and reassure them
Deploy a replacement security system for the compromised one
cards.answer: Contain the incident by pulling impacted hosts off the network
cards.why: Containment to stop further data loss and spread takes priority immediately after discovery; forensic analysis, communications, and system replacement follow once the incident is contained.

cards.q: A control only generates an alert (it does not block traffic) and inspects data after it has been decrypted on the endpoint. What type of system is this?
cards.answer: Host-based Intrusion Detection System (HIDS)
cards.why: Alert-only behavior indicates detection rather than prevention, and inspecting post-decryption data means the sensor runs on the host itself, together pointing to a HIDS.

cards.q: An organization's Maximum Tolerable Downtime is three weeks and it wants the most cost-effective recovery site with minimal upfront setup. Which site type fits?
cards.answer: Cold site
cards.why: A three-week MTD gives ample time to provision equipment at a bare facility, so the low-cost, minimal-preconfiguration cold site meets the requirement without paying for readiness that isn't needed.

cards.q: Employees are overheard discussing sensitive national-interest information on the phone in hallways and stairwells. What physical security control BEST addresses this?
options: A sensitive compartmented information facility (SCIF) for such discussions
Broader access control at building entrances
cards.answer: A sensitive compartmented information facility (SCIF) for such discussions
cards.why: A SCIF is a physically isolated, acoustically controlled space purpose-built for confidential conversations, directly closing the exposure that open hallways and stairwells create.

cards.q: In the e-discovery process for a terminated employee's mailbox, the phase where irrelevant information is filtered down to what's specifically relevant is called the ___ phase.
cards.answer: Processing
cards.why: The processing phase of e-discovery reduces the raw collected data set by filtering out irrelevant material before the narrower review and analysis phases begin.

cards.q: When using a weakness/vulnerability scoring system to prioritize remediation, which approach is most effective?
options: Prioritize vulnerabilities with both high potential impact and high likelihood of exploitation
Prioritize by likelihood of exploitation alone, regardless of impact
Prioritize by potential impact alone, regardless of likelihood
Treat every scored vulnerability with equal priority
cards.answer: Prioritize vulnerabilities with both high potential impact and high likelihood of exploitation
cards.why: Combining impact and likelihood targets remediation effort at the vulnerabilities that pose the greatest real-world risk, rather than over-weighting either factor alone or ignoring the score entirely.

cards.q: Full backups run monthly and incrementals run nightly, both at midnight. A system fails at 8:00 PM. How much data is lost?
options: 20 hours, since the last backup ran at the previous midnight
It depends entirely on when the incremental job finished
cards.answer: 20 hours, since the last backup ran at the previous midnight
cards.why: Backups capture a snapshot at the scheduled midnight run regardless of how long the job takes to complete, so anything changed between that midnight and the 8 PM failure — 20 hours — is lost.

cards.q: When designing a hot site strategy that will host only the organization's critical applications, which factor is MOST important to get right?
options: Carefully identifying and prioritizing which applications and systems are truly critical
Placing the hot site as close as possible to the primary site for easy physical access
Choosing the cheapest, lowest-spec hardware available to save costs
Locating the hot site inside the same earthquake-risk region as the primary
cards.answer: Carefully identifying and prioritizing which applications and systems are truly critical
cards.why: Since a hot site hosts only critical workloads, correctly scoping which applications qualify as critical drives everything else about its sizing and cost; siting too close to the primary defeats the purpose of geographic diversity.

cards.q: A vendor patch fixes a serious vulnerability in core banking software but is unproven and could disrupt operations. What is the best approach?
options: Submit the patch through change management, documenting the risk of applying it and of not applying it
Apply the patch immediately to production to close the vulnerability
Ignore the patch since it might be disruptive
Apply the patch only to a small non-critical subset with no formal review
cards.answer: Submit the patch through change management, documenting the risk of applying it and of not applying it
cards.why: Change management is designed to weigh competing risks like this, giving stakeholders documented visibility into both the exposure of not patching and the operational risk of an unproven patch before a decision is made.

cards.q: Detection systems confirm an advanced persistent threat on a central server and the response team is activated. What should happen immediately NEXT?
options: Begin containment to stop the threat from spreading to other systems
Deploy more IDS sensors across the network before doing anything else
Notify every employee in the company about the threat
Power the system down immediately without gathering further detail
cards.answer: Begin containment to stop the threat from spreading to other systems
cards.why: Once detection confirms an active threat, containment — such as segmentation — is the immediate next step to limit damage before broader notification, blind shutdown, or additional data-gathering.

cards.q: Which chaos engineering scenario would provide the most valuable insight into IT resiliency for a business built on a critical transactional application?
options: Simulating failure of the core database server supporting critical applications
Introducing minor graphical glitches in a non-critical internal tool
Yanking network access from one worker's personally owned laptop
Simulating a power outage at a non-critical satellite office
cards.answer: Simulating failure of the core database server supporting critical applications
cards.why: Chaos engineering delivers the most value when it targets components whose failure would have real business impact, so testing the core database behind critical applications is far more informative than testing peripheral, non-critical systems.

cards.q: Facing a surge in client-side attacks delivered via malicious websites, what is the most effective PRIMARY defensive investment?
options: Deploying robust endpoint protection across all company devices
Increasing the frequency of network penetration tests
Running mandatory employee training on spotting malicious sites
cards.answer: Deploying robust endpoint protection across all company devices
cards.why: Endpoint protection can block known-malicious sites and detect or quarantine malicious payloads at the point of execution, directly countering client-side web-based attacks better than encryption, pen testing, or training alone.

cards.q: Given problems with shared accounts, administrators having unrestricted access to logs, and no log backups, which step would do the most to strengthen accountability and auditability?
options: Restrict administrator access to logs and apply tamper-proof protections to log data
Centralize all logs into one searchable repository only
Train staff about the risks of shared accounts
Back up all logs to off-site storage
cards.answer: Restrict administrator access to logs and apply tamper-proof protections to log data
cards.why: The core accountability gap here is that even privileged users can alter evidence of their own actions, so restricting log access and making log data tamper-proof addresses that directly, beyond centralizing, training, or backing up alone.

cards.q: A FinTech CISO revising the BCP and Cyber Incident Response Plan amid a growing digital footprint should place PRIMARY focus on what?
options: Enhancing the Cyber Incident Response Plan to address cyber threats quickly and limit damage
Reviewing the Continuity of Operations Plan for day-to-day service coverage only
Updating the Crisis Communications Plan spokespeople list
Reviewing supplier dependency and building a supplier-failure backup plan
cards.answer: Enhancing the Cyber Incident Response Plan to address cyber threats quickly and limit damage
cards.why: Given the company's expanding digital footprint and sensitive financial data, the most impactful priority is strengthening the plan that directly governs rapid response to cyber threats, even though the other BCP elements still matter.

cards.q: A newly appointed continuity lead at Harborview Health is told to build the business continuity program from scratch. According to the standard four-phase BCP methodology, which activity must come first?
options: Project scope and planning, including forming the BCP team
Business impact analysis of critical functions
cards.answer: Project scope and planning, including forming the BCP team
cards.why: The four BCP phases run in order: project scope and planning, business impact analysis, continuity planning, then approval and implementation. Scoping the effort and assembling the right team must precede the BIA, because the BIA can only assess what the project has defined as in scope.

cards.q: A continuity manager wants an annual BCP exercise where department heads and key stakeholders gather in a conference room, talk through their responses to a scripted regional flood scenario, and identify gaps — without touching any production system or relocating anyone. Which exercise format matches?
cards.answer: Tabletop exercise
cards.why: A tabletop exercise gathers the team and stakeholders to reason aloud through a scripted disaster, with zero disruption to systems or operations. Parallel and full-interruption tests involve activating alternate sites or halting production, which this manager explicitly rules out.
cards.citation: SG ch.3 and ch.18 'Testing and Exercises' · outline 7.13

cards.q: During a BCP tabletop, a team discovers nobody can say where the incorporation papers, key contracts, and insurance policies would be recovered from after a headquarters fire, nor which records would even qualify as essential. Which BCP documentation component addresses exactly this gap?
options: The statement of urgency and timing
cards.answer: The vital records program
cards.why: The vital records program is the BCP subplan that identifies which records are essential to the organization's continued operation, where they are stored, and how they will be protected and recovered after a disruption. The exercise exposed its absence, which is precisely what exercises are for.

cards.q: A plant supervisor asks what her night-shift operators should actually do in the first minutes of a major disruption — who to notify, and which immediate steps to take to protect people and limit damage — before any recovery team arrives. Which BCP documentation component provides this?
cards.answer: The emergency response guidelines
cards.why: Emergency response guidelines are the BCP subplan giving on-shift personnel their immediate actions when a disruption strikes: notification lists, first-response steps, and secondary actions to take while response teams mobilize. The BIA and governance statements set priorities and accountability, not minute-one actions.

cards.q: A desktop team must roll out 400 new workstations and wants every machine to arrive with identical hardened settings, no default passwords, and only approved services enabled — while also cutting deployment hours. Within configuration management, what practice best delivers both goals?
options: Deploying every workstation from an approved baseline image
Letting each technician harden machines by hand from a checklist
Shipping vendor-default installs and patching them during the first month
Enabling all services initially and disabling the unused ones after go-live
cards.answer: Deploying every workstation from an approved baseline image
cards.why: Baseline images guarantee that desired security settings are configured correctly and identically on every deployed system, and they cut deployment and maintenance time. Manual hardening invites inconsistency, and default configurations are exactly what provisioning is supposed to eliminate.

cards.q: During an outage postmortem, engineers discover a sysadmin had quietly reconfigured a database server months earlier to fix a performance issue; the recovery team rebuilt the server from documentation that no longer matched reality, extending downtime. From a configuration management standpoint, what failure caused this?
options: The change was made without updating the configuration documentation and baseline records
The server should never have been performance-tuned at all
The recovery team should have ignored documentation and guessed the settings
Configuration management does not cover database servers
cards.answer: The change was made without updating the configuration documentation and baseline records
cards.why: Configuration management maintains system integrity by controlling and recording changes across the lifecycle, so documentation always reflects the actual deployed state. An undocumented change breaks that guarantee, and the damage typically surfaces during recovery, when teams rebuild from records that no longer match the system.

cards.q: An operations team pushes monthly patches through an automated deployment tool and assumes the job is done when the tool reports success. Last quarter an attacker exploited a server the tool had silently failed to update. Which step of an effective patch management program was missing?
options: Verifying deployment by regularly auditing and scanning systems to confirm patches actually applied
Evaluating whether the patches applied to the environment
Testing patches on isolated non-production systems
Obtaining change management approval before deployment
cards.answer: Verifying deployment by regularly auditing and scanning systems to confirm patches actually applied
cards.why: Patch management ends with verification: regularly testing and auditing systems to ensure they remain patched, because deployment tooling can fail silently. Vulnerability scans serve as an effective independent check on the patch program — evaluation, testing, and approval all happened here; verification did not.

cards.q: A DR coordinator distributes copies of the disaster recovery plan to every team member for individual review before the annual planning cycle. Beyond refreshing responsibilities, what additional organizational problem does this simple exercise reliably surface?
options: Recovery duties still assigned to personnel who have since left the company
Undersized generator fuel contracts at the alternate site
Network latency between the primary and recovery data centers
Whether the alternate site can bear full production load
cards.answer: Recovery duties still assigned to personnel who have since left the company
cards.why: A read-through test refreshes each member's awareness of their duties, lets them flag obsolete content, and — critically — identifies situations where a responsible individual has left the organization so the duty can be reassigned. Load, latency, and fuel questions require parallel or full-interruption testing.

cards.q: An audit finds that one storage engineer can both run the nightly backups and purge the audit logs that record backup activity, meaning he could exfiltrate data and erase the trail alone. Which principle is being violated?
cards.answer: Segregation of duties
cards.why: Segregation of duties ensures no single person controls every step of a critical function, so unauthorized activity requires collusion. Combining data access with the power to erase its audit trail concentrates total control in one individual, which is exactly what SoD divides among multiple trusted people.

cards.q: A PAM administrator configures the emergency break-glass account so its password is generated in two halves, each sealed and held by a different senior engineer; neither half works alone. Which control concept does this arrangement implement?
cards.answer: Split knowledge
cards.why: Split knowledge divides the information needed to perform a sensitive operation among two or more people so no individual alone can complete it, blending separation of duties with two-person control. M-of-N key recovery and split passwords are classic examples.

cards.q: A database analyst has changed teams three times in five years, and a review shows she still holds every permission from every previous role, far beyond what her current duties require. Which practice BEST corrects and prevents this condition?
options: Periodic access reviews that strip entitlements back to current job needs
Requiring a second approver for each of her future queries
Moving her accounts to a honeypot for observation
Re-imaging her workstation to a hardened baseline
cards.answer: Periodic access reviews that strip entitlements back to current job needs
cards.why: The accumulation of stale permissions across role changes is privilege creep, a violation of least privilege. Recurring entitlement reviews that re-align access to the current well-defined job function are the standard remedy; the other options address different problems entirely.

cards.q: A finance director worries that a long-tenured payments clerk could be quietly manipulating transactions for years without anyone noticing. She wants a personnel control that provides peer review of the clerk's work, cross-trains staff, and deters and detects long-running fraud. Which control fits?
options: Single sign-on for the payments platform
cards.answer: Job rotation
cards.why: Rotating employees through duties puts fresh eyes on each role's work, so schemes that depend on one person permanently controlling a task surface when someone else takes it over. Job rotation therefore deters fraud and helps detect it, while also building cross-trained coverage.

cards.q: Smoke begins pouring from a rack row while an operator is alone in the server room. The nightly backup job is mid-run, and he hesitates: aborting means losing hours of work, and the tape library is within reach. What should he do FIRST?
options: Evacuate immediately, because human life takes priority over every asset
Pull the tapes from the library so the backups survive the fire
Stay to gracefully shut down the servers before leaving
Photograph the rack for the insurance claim before exiting
cards.answer: Evacuate immediately, because human life takes priority over every asset
cards.why: Protecting people comes before protecting anything else, in every circumstance: life safety always outranks data, equipment, and recovery objectives. Every other option trades human safety for property, which no continuity or backup goal can justify.

cards.q: A lone night guard accidentally leans on the silent alarm at his post. When the monitoring center calls back, he answers calmly and includes the agreed phrase confirming the alert was unintentional. What kind of safety mechanism is the organization operating?
options: A duress system with a code word for accidental activation
A fail-secure door control with manual override
A CCTV motion-detection loop with operator callback
An uninterruptible power supply self-test routine
cards.answer: A duress system with a code word for accidental activation
cards.why: Duress systems let personnel, especially those working alone, summon help silently. Pre-arranged code words distinguish a genuine emergency from an accidental trigger: including the word stands the response down, while omitting it during an apparently calm call still keys a real response.

cards.q: An executive is about to travel to a country known for aggressive corporate espionage, including tampering with devices left in hotel rooms. Which preparation BEST protects both the executive and company data?
options: Issue a clean loaner device holding no sensitive data and require the corporate VPN over any network
Have her carry her normal laptop but rely on hotel wi-fi only when it is password-protected
Copy sensitive files to a personal tablet as a backup in case the laptop is seized
Disable the device's screen lock so border officials have no reason to detain her
cards.answer: Issue a clean loaner device holding no sensitive data and require the corporate VPN over any network
cards.why: Safe-travel practice keeps sensitive data off devices that cross high-risk borders, assumes hotel rooms and free wi-fi may be monitored, and tunnels all traffic through an employer-provided VPN. The other options either expose data to seizure and interception or actively weaken device protection.

cards.q: Several employees report waves of authentication push notifications on their phones late at night, though they were not logging in. One admits he finally tapped approve just to silence his phone. What should the security awareness program teach as the correct response to prompts a user did not initiate?
options: Never approve them, and report the unexpected prompts to security immediately
Approve once to stop the noise, then change the password in the morning
Silence notifications from the authenticator app during off-hours
Uninstall the authenticator and fall back to password-only sign-in
cards.answer: Never approve them, and report the unexpected prompts to security immediately
cards.why: This is an MFA fatigue attack: an attacker who already holds the password bombards the user with push requests hoping one gets approved. Training must make it reflexive to deny unexpected prompts and report them, since a single approval hands over the account; weakening or removing MFA makes things worse.

cards.q: A defense contractor's single perimeter fence generates constant false alarms as deer brush against its touch sensors, and guards have started ignoring alerts. Which upgrade addresses both the nuisance alarms and the need for high-security perimeter detection?
options: A PIDAS arrangement of two or three fences, with an outer fence keeping animals off the sensored main fence
Removing the touch sensors and relying on taller razor wire alone
Painting boundary stripes on the ground to mark the legal property line
Replacing the fence with additional interior CCTV cameras
cards.answer: A PIDAS arrangement of two or three fences, with an outer fence keeping animals off the sensored main fence
cards.why: A perimeter intrusion detection and assessment system layers multiple fences: the exterior fence screens out animals and casual trespassers so the sensored main fence sees far fewer false triggers, cutting the nuisance alarm rate while the corridor between fences supports patrols. The other options remove detection or ignore the perimeter entirely.

cards.q: A threat assessment for a downtown data center flags the glass lobby, which sits a few meters from the street, as vulnerable to a vehicle being deliberately driven through it. Which physical control MOST directly counters this specific threat?
options: Security bollards placed between the roadway and the entrance
An access control vestibule inside the lobby doors
Brighter exterior lighting around the entrance
A turnstile at the reception desk
cards.answer: Security bollards placed between the roadway and the entrance
cards.why: Bollards exist precisely to stop vehicles from ramming access points and entrances. Vestibules and turnstiles control pedestrian piggybacking, and lighting deters casual intruders, but none of them physically arrests a moving vehicle.

cards.q: A seized laptop passes through three analysts during an internal investigation, but nobody recorded who took possession, when, or where it was stored between handoffs. If the case goes to court, what is the MOST likely consequence?
options: The laptop may be ruled inadmissible because the chain of custody cannot be established
The laptop remains fully admissible since it was in company hands throughout
The court will simply require the first analyst to testify about its contents
The evidence converts from real evidence to documentary evidence
cards.answer: The laptop may be ruled inadmissible because the chain of custody cannot be established
cards.why: Real evidence must be authenticated, typically through a documented chain of custody recording who collected and handled it, when, and where at every transfer. Gaps in that record let opposing counsel argue the evidence could have been altered, jeopardizing its admissibility regardless of who employed the handlers.

cards.q: At 02:00 a production outage forces an on-call engineer to change a load balancer setting immediately, with no time for the normal approval workflow. The fix works. What must happen next for the change to satisfy change management?
options: Document the emergency change retroactively and submit it for after-the-fact review and approval
Nothing further, since emergency changes are exempt from the process
Roll the fix back at start of business so it can be re-applied through the normal workflow
Quietly fold the change into the next scheduled maintenance record
cards.answer: Document the emergency change retroactively and submit it for after-the-fact review and approval
cards.why: Emergency change procedures allow acting first when an outage demands it, but the process still requires the change to be documented and reviewed afterward, so the configuration record stays accurate and the change receives the scrutiny it skipped. Exempting or hiding it defeats change control; rolling back a working fix reintroduces the outage risk for no benefit.

cards.q: An auditor finds boxes of backup tapes stacked in an unventilated storeroom that swings between hot, humid summers and cold winters. Which loss are temperature and humidity controls in a media storage location chiefly meant to prevent?
options: Loss of availability through corruption of the stored media
Loss of confidentiality through electromagnetic emanation
Loss of integrity through unauthorized modification by insiders
Loss of accountability through missing access logs
cards.answer: Loss of availability through corruption of the stored media
cards.why: Media storage locations require temperature and humidity controls specifically to prevent losses due to media corruption; environmental extremes degrade magnetic and optical media until the data on them can no longer be read.

cards.q: A media librarian institutes a check-in/check-out process for portable drives and runs a secure zeroization pass on every drive when it is returned. Which risk does the sanitization step on return specifically address?
options: Recovery of data remnants when the drive is later reissued
Physical theft of the drive while it is checked out
Malware infection of the librarian's tracking workstation
Exceeding the drive's mean time between failures
cards.answer: Recovery of data remnants when the drive is later reissued
cards.why: Reusable media carries residual data from its previous assignment; sanitizing (zeroizing) drives at check-in ensures the next borrower cannot recover remnants of the prior user's data, a distinct control from the check-out tracking that deters theft.

cards.q: A records manager must pick storage media for financial archives that regulators can demand at any point over the next decade. Beyond capacity and cost, which reliability metric belongs in the media evaluation?
options: Mean time between failures of the media
Clock speed of the archival server's CPU
Annualized rate of occurrence for facility fires
Recovery time objective of the payroll application
cards.answer: Mean time between failures of the media
cards.why: Expected reliability, expressed as MTBF, belongs in any media selection for valuable or sensitive records: it indicates how long the media should remain dependable, which drives refresh cycles for long-retention archives alongside durability, format, and confidentiality needs.

cards.q: A courier service moves weekly backup tapes to an offsite vault. Management asks which single control BEST protects the data's confidentiality if a tape goes missing in transit. What should the security engineer recommend?
options: Encrypting the data written to the tapes
Requiring the courier to sign a nondisclosure agreement
Labeling each tape with its classification level
Increasing the frequency of tape rotation
cards.answer: Encrypting the data written to the tapes
cards.why: Media protection includes securing data at rest through encryption; a lost or stolen tape whose contents are strongly encrypted discloses nothing useful, whereas labels, contracts, and rotation schedules do not stop whoever holds the tape from reading it.

cards.q: SOC analysts are drowning in SIEM alerts that keep proving benign, and morale is slipping. The SOC lead orders a tuning effort. What must the tuning balance to be judged successful?
options: Reducing false positives without introducing false negatives on genuine malicious activity
Cutting total alert volume to a fixed daily quota regardless of content
Eliminating all alerting on internal traffic to focus on the perimeter
Routing every alert to an external provider so analysts see none
cards.answer: Reducing false positives without introducing false negatives on genuine malicious activity
cards.why: SIEM tuning means driving down the false-positive rate that causes analyst fatigue while never buying that quiet at the price of false negatives — silently dropping a genuine malicious event is a worse failure than the noise the effort set out to fix.

cards.q: An incident-response team has a written checklist describing how to respond to phishing reports and now wants those steps executed automatically by their SOAR platform. Which artifact translates the documented steps into automated actions?
cards.answer: A runbook
cards.why: In SOAR terminology the playbook is the document defining how to respond to an incident, while the runbook implements the playbook's documented process, translating its steps into automated actions the platform executes — cutting analyst workload and human error.

cards.q: A security team proposes standing up a decoy server seeded with pseudo flaws and fake data on an isolated segment. When the CIO asks what the organization actually gains, what is the BEST answer?
options: It diverts attackers from production systems while letting admins observe their techniques safely
It blocks attacks inline before they reach any production host
It guarantees prosecution because any access to it constitutes entrapment
It replaces the need for intrusion detection on the production network
cards.answer: It diverts attackers from production systems while letting admins observe their techniques safely
cards.why: A honeypot is a decoy holding no data of real value: its pseudo flaws tempt intruders into attacking it, keeping them occupied away from production while administrators observe their activity without compromising the live environment — it detects and studies attacks, it does not block them inline.

cards.q: Days after a flood, the facilities director reports 'restoration complete' — yet the business units complain their processes still are not running. In DR terminology, why can both statements be true?
options: Restoration returns the facility and environment to a workable state, while recovery returns business operations and processes to a working state
Restoration and recovery are synonyms, so one of the reports must be wrong
Restoration refers only to restoring data from backup tapes
Recovery always finishes before restoration in a proper DR sequence
cards.answer: Restoration returns the facility and environment to a workable state, while recovery returns business operations and processes to a working state
cards.why: Restoration and recovery are distinct: restoration makes the facility and its environment usable again, while recovery gets business operations and processes running — a repaired building with idle workgroups is restored but not recovered.

events.title: Reconnaissance sweep
events.text: 03:00 — A cluster of week-old lookalike domains is walking your public surface: DNS lookups, careers-page scrapes, a polite portscan that stays just under the alerting threshold. Someone is drawing a map of you.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0043, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.15 · outline 6.2

events.title: Resource development in your name
events.text: 03:10 — Intel flags fresh infrastructure staged in your name: a typosquatted package on a public registry and a signing certificate bought by a shell company. Nothing has touched you yet. It is being built to.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0042, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.2 · outline 1.11

events.title: Initial access — the lookalike portal
events.text: 03:20 — A finance analyst just entered credentials on a page that looked exactly like your SSO portal, and an inbound VPN session followed forty seconds later from an address no employee has ever used.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0001, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.2 · outline 1.12

events.title: Execution — a spreadsheet with children
events.text: 03:30 — A spreadsheet on a workstation in accounts payable just spawned a shell, and the shell spawned a script host, and the script host is pulling something down over an encrypted channel. Word documents do not usually have children.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0002, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.17 · outline 7.7

events.title: Persistence — autoruns nobody ordered
events.text: 03:40 — Change monitoring reports a new scheduled task, a fresh run key, and a service account nobody remembers creating — all in the last hour, all on machines that were clean at midnight. Someone is making sure a reboot will not evict them.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0003, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.16 · outline 7.3

events.title: Privilege escalation request
events.text: 03:50 — A helpdesk account that has never touched a server just requested a domain-admin token, citing a change window that is not on the calendar. The request is syntactically perfect. That is what worries you.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0004, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.14 · outline 5.4

events.title: Stealth — dressed as your baseline
events.text: 04:00 — Nothing is alerting, which is the problem: a review pass shows outbound traffic timed to mimic your backup jobs, binaries named one character off from system utilities, and logons that only ever occur inside business-hours noise. Somebody is dressing as your baseline.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0005, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.17 · outline 7.2

events.title: Defense impairment — eyes going dark
events.text: 04:10 — Three EDR agents went silent inside two minutes, a log-forwarding pipeline is dropping events on the floor, and someone just tried to add an exclusion path to the on-access scanner. Your eyes are being put out one by one.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0112, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.17 · outline 7.7

events.title: Credential access on the jump host
events.text: 04:20 — Memory forensics on a jump host found a credential-dumping tool parked next to lsass, and the domain controller shows a slow, patient spray against service accounts: two guesses per account per hour, forever.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0006, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.14 · outline 5.6

events.title: Discovery — a workstation gone shopping
events.text: 04:30 — A single workstation has, in the last hour, enumerated every share it can reach, queried group memberships it has no business caring about, and pinged its way across two subnets. It is not lost. It is shopping.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0007, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.17 · outline 7.2

events.title: Lateral movement across the map
events.text: 04:40 — The compromised workstation just opened admin sessions on three servers in a segment it should not be able to see, riding remote-service credentials that checked out as valid. The map you failed to defend is being walked.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0008, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.11 · outline 4.1

events.title: Collection — a suitcase in the vault
events.text: 04:50 — A staging directory is quietly filling on a file server: customer exports, key material, an HR extract — compressed, encrypted, and named to look like installer cache. Someone is packing a suitcase in your vault.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0009, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.5 · outline 2.6

events.title: Command and control heartbeat
events.text: 05:00 — Egress analytics found a heartbeat: one HTTPS request every 47 seconds to a content-delivery domain registered eleven days ago, payload sizes almost — not quite — identical. Something inside is checking in with something outside.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0011, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.12 · outline 4.2

events.title: Exfiltration at nine times normal
events.text: 05:10 — Outbound volume from the file segment is running nine times its nightly norm, chunked into polite parcels and routed through a cloud storage API your business does use — just never at 5 a.m., and never this much.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0010, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.5 · outline 2.6

events.title: Impact — the quiet part is over
events.text: 05:20 — File servers are renaming their contents with an extension you have only seen in incident reports, shadow copies are being deleted in bulk, and a text file titled HOW_TO_RECOVER just appeared in every share. The quiet part of the night is over.
events.citation: MITRE ATT&CK TA0040, attack.mitre.org · SG ch.18 · outline 7.10

events.title: Fieldwork ping — SOC 2 Type II
events.text: 03:15 — The external audit team's fieldwork portal pings: they have pulled tonight's control evidence for the service-organization report and want the operating-effectiveness samples walked through before breakfast. Type II means the whole period counts — including this shift.
events.citation: SG ch.15 · outline 6.5

events.title: Change reconciliation demand
events.text: 04:15 — Internal audit's continuous-monitoring job flagged four production changes this week with no linked approval record. They are asking the night desk to reconcile each one against the change calendar before the morning stand-up — emergency changes included.
events.citation: SG ch.16 · outline 7.9

events.title: Recertification red row
events.text: 05:30 — The quarterly access recertification came back with a red row: a departed contractor's account shows a successful logon dated three days after their exit interview. HR says leaver, the directory says active, and the reviewer wants to know which one is lying.
events.citation: SG ch.13 · outline 5.5

events.title: CISO ping — board pre-read math
events.text: 03:45 — The CISO, unable to sleep, messages the desk directly: the board pre-read is due at 08:00 and the annualized-loss figures for the top three scenarios read wrong to her. Sanity-check the exposure math before it goes to print.
events.citation: SG ch.2 · outline 1.9

events.title: Counsel joins the bridge
events.text: 04:45 — Outside counsel joins the incident bridge uninvited: if tonight's activity touched resident data from two particular jurisdictions, notification clocks may already be running, and they need the exposure scoped — what data, whose, and under which law — before advising the CEO.
events.citation: SG ch.4 · outline 1.4

events.title: The chair wants failover answers
events.text: 05:45 — A board member read about a rival's three-day outage and emailed the chair at midnight. By 05:45 it has rolled downhill to you: could we survive that, how long could finance be down, and when did we last actually test the failover rather than talk about it?
events.citation: SG ch.3 · outline 1.7
